13	
14	# Pinned Unpin Menu And Degraded Health
15	
16	## TL;DR
17	
18	<!-- bugs:block:tldr -->
19	
20	Symptom: On Amir's physical iPhone 17 Pro after app startup, five pinned rows were visible. Two could be unpinned, then the remaining three were stuck. Swiping a pinned row no longer reliably exposed the `Unpin` action; sometimes the action appeared briefly and disappeared before it could be tapped. The same clean rebuild also showed partially connected health: Dock feed degraded, thread detail degraded, archive degraded, voice degraded, and diagnostics degraded.
21	
22	Impact: Pinned rows can become effectively impossible to unpin from the primary Dock UI, and the system health UI can report broad degradation even after relays were restarted, making it unclear whether the client is live, stale, or only partially connected.
23	
24	Most likely cause: two separate client-side problems. First, the pinned section is a custom `UICollectionView` bridge that calls `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update; live Dock updates or height/layout updates during a swipe can close UIKit swipe actions, matching the "menu pops in and out" symptom. Second, the health UI is treating a capped Dock row window (`Home: Showing 250 of 964`) as global service degradation, then applying that same fallback to Dock feed, thread detail, archive, voice, and diagnostics when no route evidence has been loaded.
25	
26	Next action: propose the fix only after review. Do not patch production code yet. The physical iPhone 17 Pro is explicitly out of scope for remote commands.
27	
28	Status: root cause found; fix not implemented.
29	
30	<!-- /bugs:block:tldr -->
31	
32	## Bug North Star
33	
34	The app should let a user unpin any visible pinned Dock row with a stable, tappable action. Live stream updates, route-health refreshes, layout recalculation, worker activity, or startup recovery should not make the swipe action disappear before the user can tap it.
35	
36	The health UI should distinguish "relay process is reachable but route proof is not yet available" from true degradation. A clean rebuild against restarted healthy relays should not show every major feature as degraded unless there is concrete route-level failure evidence.
37	
38	## Scope And Constraints
39	
40	- Do not query, install to, launch on, log from, or otherwise control the physical iPhone 17 Pro during this investigation.
41	- Use source code, local relay diagnostics, logs, and the `iPhone 17` simulator for reproduction.
42	- Analyze first. Do not modify production code until the bug is fix-ready and Amir asks for the fix.
43	- Keep this document as the source of truth for evidence and decisions.
44	
45	## Evidence
46	
47	<!-- bugs:block:analysis -->
48	
49	### User-Reported Evidence
50	
51	- Physical iPhone 17 Pro cannot be remotely controlled for this diagnosis.
52	- After startup, five pinned rows were visible.
53	- Two pinned rows could be unpinned successfully.
54	- Three pinned rows remained stuck.
55	- Swiping a stuck pinned row does not reliably show the `Unpin` menu.
56	- Sometimes the `Unpin` menu appears and disappears before it can be tapped.
57	- Same app state reports partially connected health:
58	  - Dock feed degraded
59	  - Thread detail degraded
60	  - Archive degraded
61	  - Voice degraded
62	  - Diagnostics degraded
63	- This happened after a clean rebuild and relay restarts.
64	
65	### Current Repo/Runtime Baseline
66	
67	- Time captured: `2026-06-02T12:03:10Z`.
68	- Repo: `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client`.
69	- Branch commit at the time of investigation start was previously deployed as `e048b5d Unify Dock projection identity`.
70	- The first diagnostic pass used source reads only and avoided all physical-device commands after Amir unplugged the iPhone 17 Pro.
71	
72	### Runtime Evidence: Relay Health Was Not The Broad Failure
73	
74	Relay route summaries were collected from both configured hosts:
75	
76	- `http://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
77	- `http://home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
78	
79	Both relays returned `/syncz` as:
80	
81	```json
82	{"ok":true,"service":"codex-dock-relay","schema":"codexdock.syncz.v1","state":"available"}
83	```
84	
85	The route summaries did not show app-critical failures. They showed a mix of healthy exercised routes and unknown passive/manual routes:
86	
87	- `dock/resync`, `dock/subscribe`, and `initialize` had healthy evidence on at least the local host path.
88	- `dock/update`, `thread/detail/*`, archive mutation/update routes, and voice routes were mostly `unknown` because they are passive/manual routes and had not been exercised.
89	- `appCriticalFailures` was `[]` on both hosts.
90	
91	Inference: the relays were reachable. Unknown route evidence exists, but that is not the same as a failed relay. The user-visible "everything degraded" screen needed client-side explanation.
92	
93	### Simulator Evidence: Health Degradation Is A Dock Window Fallback
94	
95	The `iPhone 17` simulator was launched with:
96	
97	```bash
98	FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
99	```
100	
101	Accessibility dump evidence from the Dock screen:
102	
103	- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
104	  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=0; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; 487 shown ... Partial`
105	- `codexdock.connectivity.global` label:
106	  - `Online 2/2`
107	- `codexdock.connectivity.global` value:
108	  - `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`
109	
110	After opening System Health from the global indicator, accessibility showed:
111	
112	- Summary:
113	  - `Partial`
114	  - `Home: Showing 250 of 964`
115	- `codexdock.system-health.category.dockFeed`:
116	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
117	- `codexdock.system-health.category.threadDetail`:
118	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
119	- `codexdock.system-health.category.archive`:
120	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
121	- `codexdock.system-health.category.voice`:
122	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
123	- `codexdock.system-health.category.diagnostics`:
124	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
125	
126	Opening the `Home` host detail showed:
127	
128	- `State, Showing 250 of 964`
129	- `Technical Evidence`
130	- `No route evidence yet.`
131	
132	Conclusion: the System Health screen degraded every category without route-level evidence. It copied the global Dock row-window partial message into unrelated feature categories.
133	
134	### Code Anchor: Dock Row Windows Become Connectivity Partial
135	
136	The row-window state originates in `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`.
137	
138	Relevant source anchors:
139	
140	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:428-435`: if a stream snapshot is not complete, `hostStatus(...)` returns `.partial(rowCount: visibleRows, message: "Showing \(visibleRows) of \(knownTotal)")`.
141	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:364`: `DockRenderInput.isPartial` becomes true if any host is checking or partial.
142	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:278-296`: loaded Dock snapshots are reported to `AppConnectivityStore`.
143	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:419-437`: `.partial(_, message)` Dock host status becomes `HostConnectivityPhase.partial(message)`.
144	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:610-616`: if all hosts are online-like but at least one is partial, the global status becomes `.partial("\(host): \(message)")`.
145	
146	This means `Home: Showing 250 of 964` is currently treated as global connectivity partiality even though it is actually a data-window completeness fact.
147	
148	### Code Anchor: System Health Falls Back From Global Partial To Every Category
149	
150	Relevant source anchors:
151	
152	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:66-68`: System Health projects from `store.hosts` and `store.overallStatus`.
153	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:50-57`: route diagnostics are only fetched by tapping `Run check`; they are not fetched on open.
154	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:31-35`: if a category has no route diagnostics, it uses `fallbackStatus(for:overallStatus:)`.
155	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:78-79`: global `.partial(message)` maps to category `.degraded(message, nextAction: "Run check or open host details.")`.
156	
157	This is the exact code path that reproduced in the simulator: the `Home` row-window partial became a global `.partial`, then every category with no route evidence displayed `Degraded`.
158	
159	### Code Anchor: Pinned Rows Are A Custom UIKit Collection View
160	
161	Pinned rows do not use the normal SwiftUI `DockSwipeActionRow` path. In `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`, body rows use `dockRow(row, resetToken:)`, but pinned rows use `dockPinnedRow(row)` inside `DockPinnedSectionView`.
162	
163	Relevant source anchors:
164	
165	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:729`: renders `DockPinnedSectionView` when `projection.pinnedRows` is not empty.
166	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:733`: pinned reorder callback calls `Task { await store.reorderPinnedRows(rows) }`.
167	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:734`: pinned unpin callback calls `Task { await store.setPinned(false, for: row) }`.
168	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:859`: `dockPinnedRow(_:)` renders only `dockRowContent`, with `showsContextMenu: false`.
169	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:219`: pinned rows render through `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView`.
170	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:274`: `makeUIView` creates a `UICollectionView`.
171	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:279`: trailing swipe actions are provided by `UICollectionLayoutListConfiguration.trailingSwipeActionsConfigurationProvider`.
172	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:310`: `updateUIView` runs on SwiftUI updates.
173	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:315-320`: when not moving, `updateUIView` assigns `workingRows = rows`, calls `collectionView.reloadData()`, invalidates layout, forces layout, and reports measured height.
174	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:425-428`: the `Unpin` contextual action calls `parent.onUnpin(row)` and completes.
175	
176	First inference: any SwiftUI update to the pinned section while a UIKit trailing swipe action is open can cause `reloadData()`. UIKit list reloads close open swipe actions. This matches the user-visible symptom where the menu appears briefly and disappears.
177	
178	### Code Anchor: Body Rows Use A Separate Swipe Implementation
179	
180	Body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`, a SwiftUI view with local `offset` state.
181	
182	Relevant source anchors:
183	
184	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:8`: `DockSwipeActionRow`.
185	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:16`: local `@State private var offset`.
186	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:30`: `.simultaneousGesture(dragGesture)`.
187	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:42-50`: row ID, pin state, and render revision changes close the action.
188	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:832`: body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`.
189	
190	First inference: pinned rows and body rows use materially different interaction implementations. A bug in pinned unpin can exist even if body row pin/unpin behaves normally.
191	
192	### Code Anchor: Pin/Unpin Is Local Metadata
193	
194	Relevant source anchors:
195	
196	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:208`: `setPinned(_:for:)`.
197	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:209-215`: pin/unpin persists through `persistMetadataChange`.
198	- `CodexDock/Metadata/LocalMetadataEngine.swift:93-100`: setting pinned updates `pinnedAt` and `pinnedOrder`; unpin clears both.
199	
200	First inference: the stuck swipe menu is likely an interaction/rendering issue before the `setPinned(false, for:)` action fires. The user's report says the menu often cannot be tapped; that is different from tapping `Unpin` and having persistence fail.
201	
202	### Simulator Evidence: Five Pinned Rows Survive Startup
203	
204	The simulator initially had no metadata file:
205	
206	- App container: `.../Library/Application Support/CodexDock`
207	- `thread-metadata.json`: absent
208	
209	To approximate the physical-phone startup state without touching the physical phone, five current `Amir-M5` Dock rows were seeded into the simulator's own app data as pinned local metadata. Each entry used the real app key shape:
210	
211	- `hostID`
212	- `backendSessionID`
213	- `threadID`
214	- `isPinned`
215	- `pinnedAt`
216	- `pinnedOrder`
217	
218	After relaunching with:
219	
220	```bash
221	FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
222	```
223	
224	Accessibility showed:
225	
226	- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
227	  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=5; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; ... Partial`
228	- `codexdock.dock.pinned.toggle` value:
229	  - `Expanded, Pinned 5`
230	- `codexdock.dock.pinned.header` text:
231	  - `Pinned 5`
232	
233	Conclusion: persisted local pin metadata is loaded and projected correctly after startup in the simulator. The remaining bug is not "pins vanish on restart"; it is the pinned interaction surface becoming unstable after pins are present.
234	
235	### Simulator Evidence: Pinned Section Accessibility Shape Is Suspicious
236	
237	With five pins seeded, the accessibility tree showed:
238	
239	- Pinned header at `y=303`.
240	- Only one visible pinned row element was exposed at `y=782`.
241	- That row had value ending in `Pinned`.
242	
243	This does not by itself prove a layout bug, because accessibility listing only reports visible elements and the embedded collection is tall. But it reinforces that the pinned section is a large embedded UIKit surface with its own cell layout, not the same simple SwiftUI row stack used by body rows.
244	
245	### Testing Tool Drift: `sim-ui-dump` Contract Is Not Trustworthy Right Now
246	
247	Before seeded pins, `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` produced useful files but exited nonzero because the proof schema rejected the dump:
248	
249	```text
250	proof report contract check failed: /tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json/app: must NOT have additional properties
251	```
252	
253	This means the simulator dump producer and `contract/proof/sim-ui-dump.schema.json` have drifted. The dump still wrote:
254	
255	- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json`
256	- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.md`
257	
258	After seeding five pinned rows, a second `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` hung during the current visible screen XCTest path and had to be killed. The lower-level Mobile MCP accessibility dump still worked and captured the pinned state. This is relevant because the formal proof path is currently weak around exactly the UI state under investigation.
259	
260	## Investigation Log
261	
262	### 2026-06-02T12:03Z Initial Source Triage
263	
264	Actions:
265	
266	- Confirmed active goal and physical iPhone 17 Pro no-touch constraint.
267	- Searched source for `pin`, `pinned`, `unpin`, `swipeActions`, `contextMenu`, degraded health, and route-health terms.
268	- Read `DockPinnedViews.swift`, `DockView.swift`, `DockStore.swift`, and `DockCardProjection.swift`.
269	
270	Learned:
271	
272	- Pinned rows are implemented as a custom UIKit `UICollectionView` list with trailing swipe actions and long-press reorder.
273	- Pinned rows call `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update when not actively moving.
274	- Body rows use a separate SwiftUI offset-based swipe row and are not equivalent to pinned rows.
275	- Pinned row content intentionally disables the normal context menu.
276	- Unpin persistence is local metadata; the observed failure is probably before persistence because the action cannot be stably tapped.
277	
278	### 2026-06-02T12:07Z Relay And Health Evidence
279	
280	Actions:
281	
282	- Queried local and home relay health endpoints.
283	- Opened System Health in the `iPhone 17` simulator through accessibility, not screenshots.
284	- Opened `Home` host detail inside System Health.
285	- Read `ThreadCardTable`, `AppConnectivityStore`, `SystemHealthView`, and `SystemHealthProjector`.
286	
287	Learned:
288	
289	- Relays were reachable and `/syncz` returned `state=available`.
290	- The simulator global indicator showed `Online 2/2`, but value `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
291	- System Health showed every category degraded for the same reason: `Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
292	- The `Home` host detail said `No route evidence yet.`
293	- Code confirms route diagnostics are not auto-fetched when System Health opens; the `Run check` button is the fetch path.
294	- Code confirms global `.partial` falls back to category `.degraded` when a category has no route evidence.
295	
296	Conclusion:
297	
298	The broad degraded UI is a client classification bug. A capped Dock row window is being presented as feature degradation across unrelated categories.
299	
300	### 2026-06-02T12:11Z Simulator Pinned-State Reproduction
301	
302	Actions:
303	
304	- Confirmed simulator app data had no existing `thread-metadata.json`.
305	- Fetched current Dock cards from the relay card stream to avoid guessing metadata keys.
306	- Seeded five simulator-only local metadata pins using real `hostID/backendSessionID/threadID` keys.
307	- Relaunched the app with `FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'`.
308	- Dumped visible simulator accessibility via Mobile MCP against the simulator UDID.
309	
310	Learned:
311	
312	- The simulator Dock loaded with `pinned=5`.
313	- The pinned header displayed `Pinned 5`.
314	- At least one pinned row was visible and carried accessibility value `Pinned`.
315	- Pin persistence and projection survived restart.
316	
317	Conclusion:
318	
319	The remaining pinned problem is focused on the interaction layer: exposing and tapping `Unpin` on pinned rows.
320	
321	### 2026-06-02T12:13Z Formal UI Dump Gap
322	
323	Actions:
324	
325	- Ran `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` after seeded pins.
326	- Stopped the dump after it hung.
327	
328	Learned:
329	
330	- The first dump before seeded pins already revealed schema drift: top-level `app` exists in produced JSON but is rejected by the proof schema.
331	- The second dump hung in `CodexDockCurrentUIDumpTests/testDumpsCurrentVisibleScreenOnce`; only config was written under `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T121309Z/`.
332	- Mobile MCP accessibility dumping still worked.
333	
334	Conclusion:
335	
336	Our simulator proof path has blind spots in this class of bug. It can fail schema validation or hang in the precise pinned/high-text accessibility state we need to diagnose.
337	
338	## Ranked Hypotheses
339	
340	### H1: Pinned UIKit `reloadData()` closes swipe actions during live updates
341	
342	Confidence: high after source triage plus simulator pinned-state reproduction; not yet instrumented with a swipe-open timestamp.
343	
344	Mechanism:
345	
346	- User swipes a pinned row.
347	- UIKit opens the trailing `Unpin` action.
348	- A live Dock update, projection revision, health state update, height measurement callback, or other SwiftUI state change re-runs `updateUIView`.
349	- `updateUIView` calls `collectionView.reloadData()`.
350	- UIKit closes the open swipe action.
351	- User sees the menu pop in and out before it can be tapped.
352	
353	Why it fits:
354	
355	- The symptom is instability of the menu, not a failed `Unpin` action after tap.
356	- It can be worse after startup, when streams/health/status updates are still settling.
357	- It can be worse with live work happening, because updates keep arriving.
358	- It is specific to pinned rows because pinned rows use a collection view bridge.
359	
360	What would prove it:
361	
362	- Simulator reproduction where opening a pinned-row swipe action followed by a live Dock update or forced render update closes the action.
363	- Logs/instrumentation showing `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView.updateUIView`/`reloadData()` happens while the swipe action is open.
364	- A UI dump or XCTest proof showing `Unpin` action appears and disappears across samples without user tapping it.
365	
366	Current evidence:
367	
368	- The exact code path calls `collectionView.reloadData()` on every `updateUIView` while not moving.
369	- The simulator reproduced the same five-pinned startup state.
370	- The app is live and continuously receiving Dock stream/health changes.
371	- UIKit list reloads are known to close active cell swipe actions.
372	
373	This is the most direct explanation for the reported "appears then disappears" menu behavior.
374	
375	### H2: Long-press reorder recognizer competes with swipe recognizer
376	
377	Confidence: medium.
378	
379	Mechanism:
380	
381	- Pinned rows add a `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` for drag reorder with `minimumPressDuration = 0.35`.
382	- The recognizer has `cancelsTouchesInView = true`.
383	- Gesture delegate returns false for simultaneous recognition when either gesture is a long press.
384	- Slow/hesitant swipes could be interpreted as long press/reorder attempts, canceling the swipe action.
385	
386	Why it fits:
387	
388	- User describes inconsistent menu behavior.
389	- Pinned rows uniquely combine swipe actions and long-press reordering.
390	
391	What would prove it:
392	
393	- Simulator reproduction where slow swipes fail but fast swipes work.
394	- Gesture logs showing long-press began/canceled near failed swipe attempts.
395	
396	### H3: Hidden pinned rows by filter/scope are being mistaken for stuck pinned rows
397	
398	Confidence: low-medium.
399	
400	Mechanism:
401	
402	- `DockCardProjection` computes `pinnedRows` only from filtered rows.
403	- `allPinnedRows` includes all pinned rows.
404	- If filters/scope hide pinned rows, header can show `Pinned X of Y`.
405	
406	Why it partially fits:
407	
408	- User had five pinned, then two unpinned, leaving three.
409	- Existing UI has hidden pinned summary paths.
410	
411	Why it does not fit well:
412	
413	- User says the three rows are visible and swipe actions are unstable, not hidden.
414	- This does not explain the swipe menu appearing and disappearing.
415	
416	What would prove/disprove it:
417	
418	- UI dump showing header/title, visible pinned row count, active filters, and actual pinned summary.
419	
420	### H4: Unpin persistence fails after tap
421	
422	Confidence: low based on current report.
423	
424	Mechanism:
425	
426	- `metadataEngine.setPinned(false, for:)` throws.
427	- `persistMetadataChange` sets an action error and pinned state remains.
428	
429	Why it does not fit well:
430	
431	- User specifically reports not getting a stable unpin menu.
432	- Need evidence of a tap completing and a persistence error before elevating this.
433	
434	What would prove it:
435	
436	- `DockLog` action error or metadata write error after tapping `Unpin`.
437	
438	### H5: Health categories are degraded because route health is unproven/unknown after restart
439	
440	Confidence: superseded.
441	
442	This was the first health hypothesis, but the simulator proved a different specific path. Unknown route evidence is real, but unknown-only diagnostics are not what caused the observed broad degraded labels. The observed labels happened because no route evidence had been loaded into the System Health view, so it fell back from global `.partial`.
443	
444	### H6: Dock row-window partiality is incorrectly reused as broad service degradation
445	
446	Confidence: high; reproduced in simulator and confirmed in code.
447	
448	Mechanism:
449	
450	- Home relay has more rows than the current Dock stream window limit.
451	- `ThreadCardTable.hostStatus(...)` returns `.partial(rowCount: 250, message: "Showing 250 of 964")`.
452	- `AppConnectivityStore.reportDockState` records that as `HostConnectivityPhase.partial("Showing 250 of 964")`.
453	- Overall connectivity becomes `.partial("Home: Showing 250 of 964")`.
454	- System Health opens without route diagnostics because `refreshRelayDiagnostics()` only runs from `Run check`.
455	- `SystemHealthProjector` sees no category route diagnostics and maps global `.partial` to `.degraded` for every category.
456	
457	Why it fits:
458	
459	- Simulator exactly displayed this state.
460	- Host detail exactly showed `No route evidence yet`.
461	- Every category used the same Dock window message.
462	- Relay `/syncz` was available and app-critical failures were empty.
463	
464	What would prove it further:
465	
466	- A unit test where `SystemHealthProjector.snapshot(hosts: [Home partial window], overallStatus: .partial("Home: Showing 250 of 964"))` with empty `routeDiagnostics` proves every category is currently degraded.
467	- A corrected test where row-window partiality no longer maps to service degradation.
468	
469	## Verification Plan
470	
471	1. Inspect health category mapping in Swift and route-health semantics in relay scripts.
472	2. Capture current local and home relay `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and `/syncz` payload summaries.
473	3. Run `rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'` or `FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'` as needed.
474	4. Use simulator UI dump before and after pinning/unpinning where possible:
475	   - `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'`
476	5. Create or use existing UI automation/accessibility path to pin several rows, restart/relaunch the simulator app, and sample pinned-row action visibility.
477	6. Capture simulator logs:
478	   - `rtk make sim-logs SIM='iPhone 17'`
479	7. Update this doc with proved root cause, disproved theories, and fix-ready status only when evidence is strong.

481	## Fix Plan
482	
483	<!-- bugs:block:fix_plan -->
484	
485	Not implemented. Proposed shape for review:
486	
487	1. Split "Dock data window is partial" from "connectivity/service health is degraded."
488	   - `Showing 250 of 964` is a Dock data completeness/status message.
489	   - It should not drive global connectivity or System Health feature degradation by itself.
490	   - Keep the message visible in Dock where row-window completeness matters.
491	2. Make System Health route-evidence based.
492	   - Opening System Health should either fetch route diagnostics automatically or clearly show `Not checked` until the user runs a check.
493	   - A category should be `Degraded` only for direct failed/degraded/stale evidence in that category, not because Dock has a capped row window.
494	3. Replace the pinned row interaction path with one stable implementation.
495	   - Preferred permanent fix: stop using the custom embedded `UICollectionView` for pinned rows if reorder can be achieved with a SwiftUI-native list/stack path, or at least stop unconditional `reloadData()` during normal updates.
496	   - If keeping UIKit temporarily, update only changed rows with diffable data source or batch updates and never call `reloadData()` while a swipe action is open.
497	   - Reevaluate the long-press reorder recognizer so it does not cancel swipe actions.
498	4. Add tests for live-like behavior, not static snapshots only.
499	   - Pinned row UI test: seed or pin 5 rows, relaunch, open a pinned row swipe action, inject/replay a Dock update, assert `Unpin` remains visible long enough to tap.
500	   - Health projector test: capped Dock row window does not mark thread detail/archive/voice/diagnostics degraded.
501	   - System Health UI/accessibility test: with no route evidence, categories show `Not checked` or route-specific healthy/degraded states, not copied Dock window text.

title: Pinned unpin menu instability and degraded health on clean rebuild
date: 2026-06-02
status: root-cause-found

  - ../CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md

# Pinned Unpin Menu And Degraded Health

## TL;DR

<!-- bugs:block:tldr -->

Symptom: On Amir's physical iPhone 17 Pro after app startup, five pinned rows were visible. Two could be unpinned, then the remaining three were stuck. Swiping a pinned row no longer reliably exposed the `Unpin` action; sometimes the action appeared briefly and disappeared before it could be tapped. The same clean rebuild also showed partially connected health: Dock feed degraded, thread detail degraded, archive degraded, voice degraded, and diagnostics degraded.

Impact: Pinned rows can become effectively impossible to unpin from the primary Dock UI, and the system health UI can report broad degradation even after relays were restarted, making it unclear whether the client is live, stale, or only partially connected.

Most likely cause: two separate client-side problems. First, the pinned section is a custom `UICollectionView` bridge that calls `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update; live Dock updates or height/layout updates during a swipe can close UIKit swipe actions, matching the "menu pops in and out" symptom. Second, the health UI is treating a capped Dock row window (`Home: Showing 250 of 964`) as global service degradation, then applying that same fallback to Dock feed, thread detail, archive, voice, and diagnostics when no route evidence has been loaded.

Next action: propose the fix only after review. Do not patch production code yet. The physical iPhone 17 Pro is explicitly out of scope for remote commands.

Status: root cause found; fix not implemented.

<!-- /bugs:block:tldr -->

## Bug North Star

The app should let a user unpin any visible pinned Dock row with a stable, tappable action. Live stream updates, route-health refreshes, layout recalculation, worker activity, or startup recovery should not make the swipe action disappear before the user can tap it.

The health UI should distinguish "relay process is reachable but route proof is not yet available" from true degradation. A clean rebuild against restarted healthy relays should not show every major feature as degraded unless there is concrete route-level failure evidence.

## Scope And Constraints

- Do not query, install to, launch on, log from, or otherwise control the physical iPhone 17 Pro during this investigation.
- Use source code, local relay diagnostics, logs, and the `iPhone 17` simulator for reproduction.
- Analyze first. Do not modify production code until the bug is fix-ready and Amir asks for the fix.
- Keep this document as the source of truth for evidence and decisions.

## Evidence

<!-- bugs:block:analysis -->

### User-Reported Evidence

- Physical iPhone 17 Pro cannot be remotely controlled for this diagnosis.
- After startup, five pinned rows were visible.
- Two pinned rows could be unpinned successfully.
- Three pinned rows remained stuck.
- Swiping a stuck pinned row does not reliably show the `Unpin` menu.
- Sometimes the `Unpin` menu appears and disappears before it can be tapped.
- Same app state reports partially connected health:
  - Dock feed degraded
  - Thread detail degraded
  - Archive degraded
  - Voice degraded
  - Diagnostics degraded
- This happened after a clean rebuild and relay restarts.

### Current Repo/Runtime Baseline

- Time captured: `2026-06-02T12:03:10Z`.
- Repo: `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client`.
- Branch commit at the time of investigation start was previously deployed as `e048b5d Unify Dock projection identity`.
- The first diagnostic pass used source reads only and avoided all physical-device commands after Amir unplugged the iPhone 17 Pro.

### Runtime Evidence: Relay Health Was Not The Broad Failure

Relay route summaries were collected from both configured hosts:

- `http://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
- `http://home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`

Both relays returned `/syncz` as:

```json
{"ok":true,"service":"codex-dock-relay","schema":"codexdock.syncz.v1","state":"available"}
```

The route summaries did not show app-critical failures. They showed a mix of healthy exercised routes and unknown passive/manual routes:

- `dock/resync`, `dock/subscribe`, and `initialize` had healthy evidence on at least the local host path.
- `dock/update`, `thread/detail/*`, archive mutation/update routes, and voice routes were mostly `unknown` because they are passive/manual routes and had not been exercised.
- `appCriticalFailures` was `[]` on both hosts.

Inference: the relays were reachable. Unknown route evidence exists, but that is not the same as a failed relay. The user-visible "everything degraded" screen needed client-side explanation.

### Simulator Evidence: Health Degradation Is A Dock Window Fallback

The `iPhone 17` simulator was launched with:

```bash
FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
```

Accessibility dump evidence from the Dock screen:

- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=0; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; 487 shown ... Partial`
- `codexdock.connectivity.global` label:
  - `Online 2/2`
- `codexdock.connectivity.global` value:
  - `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`

After opening System Health from the global indicator, accessibility showed:

- Summary:
  - `Partial`
  - `Home: Showing 250 of 964`
- `codexdock.system-health.category.dockFeed`:
  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
- `codexdock.system-health.category.threadDetail`:
  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
- `codexdock.system-health.category.archive`:
  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
- `codexdock.system-health.category.voice`:
  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
- `codexdock.system-health.category.diagnostics`:
  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`

Opening the `Home` host detail showed:

- `State, Showing 250 of 964`
- `Technical Evidence`
- `No route evidence yet.`

Conclusion: the System Health screen degraded every category without route-level evidence. It copied the global Dock row-window partial message into unrelated feature categories.

### Code Anchor: Dock Row Windows Become Connectivity Partial

The row-window state originates in `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`.

Relevant source anchors:

- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:428-435`: if a stream snapshot is not complete, `hostStatus(...)` returns `.partial(rowCount: visibleRows, message: "Showing \(visibleRows) of \(knownTotal)")`.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:364`: `DockRenderInput.isPartial` becomes true if any host is checking or partial.
- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:278-296`: loaded Dock snapshots are reported to `AppConnectivityStore`.
- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:419-437`: `.partial(_, message)` Dock host status becomes `HostConnectivityPhase.partial(message)`.
- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:610-616`: if all hosts are online-like but at least one is partial, the global status becomes `.partial("\(host): \(message)")`.

This means `Home: Showing 250 of 964` is currently treated as global connectivity partiality even though it is actually a data-window completeness fact.

### Code Anchor: System Health Falls Back From Global Partial To Every Category

Relevant source anchors:

- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:66-68`: System Health projects from `store.hosts` and `store.overallStatus`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:50-57`: route diagnostics are only fetched by tapping `Run check`; they are not fetched on open.
- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:31-35`: if a category has no route diagnostics, it uses `fallbackStatus(for:overallStatus:)`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:78-79`: global `.partial(message)` maps to category `.degraded(message, nextAction: "Run check or open host details.")`.

This is the exact code path that reproduced in the simulator: the `Home` row-window partial became a global `.partial`, then every category with no route evidence displayed `Degraded`.

### Code Anchor: Pinned Rows Are A Custom UIKit Collection View

Pinned rows do not use the normal SwiftUI `DockSwipeActionRow` path. In `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`, body rows use `dockRow(row, resetToken:)`, but pinned rows use `dockPinnedRow(row)` inside `DockPinnedSectionView`.

Relevant source anchors:

- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:729`: renders `DockPinnedSectionView` when `projection.pinnedRows` is not empty.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:733`: pinned reorder callback calls `Task { await store.reorderPinnedRows(rows) }`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:734`: pinned unpin callback calls `Task { await store.setPinned(false, for: row) }`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:859`: `dockPinnedRow(_:)` renders only `dockRowContent`, with `showsContextMenu: false`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:219`: pinned rows render through `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:274`: `makeUIView` creates a `UICollectionView`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:279`: trailing swipe actions are provided by `UICollectionLayoutListConfiguration.trailingSwipeActionsConfigurationProvider`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:310`: `updateUIView` runs on SwiftUI updates.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:315-320`: when not moving, `updateUIView` assigns `workingRows = rows`, calls `collectionView.reloadData()`, invalidates layout, forces layout, and reports measured height.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:425-428`: the `Unpin` contextual action calls `parent.onUnpin(row)` and completes.

First inference: any SwiftUI update to the pinned section while a UIKit trailing swipe action is open can cause `reloadData()`. UIKit list reloads close open swipe actions. This matches the user-visible symptom where the menu appears briefly and disappears.

### Code Anchor: Body Rows Use A Separate Swipe Implementation

Body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`, a SwiftUI view with local `offset` state.

Relevant source anchors:

- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:8`: `DockSwipeActionRow`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:16`: local `@State private var offset`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:30`: `.simultaneousGesture(dragGesture)`.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:42-50`: row ID, pin state, and render revision changes close the action.
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:832`: body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`.

First inference: pinned rows and body rows use materially different interaction implementations. A bug in pinned unpin can exist even if body row pin/unpin behaves normally.

### Code Anchor: Pin/Unpin Is Local Metadata

Relevant source anchors:

- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:208`: `setPinned(_:for:)`.
- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:209-215`: pin/unpin persists through `persistMetadataChange`.
- `CodexDock/Metadata/LocalMetadataEngine.swift:93-100`: setting pinned updates `pinnedAt` and `pinnedOrder`; unpin clears both.

First inference: the stuck swipe menu is likely an interaction/rendering issue before the `setPinned(false, for:)` action fires. The user's report says the menu often cannot be tapped; that is different from tapping `Unpin` and having persistence fail.

### Simulator Evidence: Five Pinned Rows Survive Startup

The simulator initially had no metadata file:

- App container: `.../Library/Application Support/CodexDock`
- `thread-metadata.json`: absent

To approximate the physical-phone startup state without touching the physical phone, five current `Amir-M5` Dock rows were seeded into the simulator's own app data as pinned local metadata. Each entry used the real app key shape:

- `hostID`
- `backendSessionID`
- `threadID`
- `isPinned`
- `pinnedAt`
- `pinnedOrder`

After relaunching with:

```bash
FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
```

Accessibility showed:

- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=5; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; ... Partial`
- `codexdock.dock.pinned.toggle` value:
  - `Expanded, Pinned 5`
- `codexdock.dock.pinned.header` text:
  - `Pinned 5`

Conclusion: persisted local pin metadata is loaded and projected correctly after startup in the simulator. The remaining bug is not "pins vanish on restart"; it is the pinned interaction surface becoming unstable after pins are present.

### Simulator Evidence: Pinned Section Accessibility Shape Is Suspicious

With five pins seeded, the accessibility tree showed:

- Pinned header at `y=303`.
- Only one visible pinned row element was exposed at `y=782`.
- That row had value ending in `Pinned`.

This does not by itself prove a layout bug, because accessibility listing only reports visible elements and the embedded collection is tall. But it reinforces that the pinned section is a large embedded UIKit surface with its own cell layout, not the same simple SwiftUI row stack used by body rows.

### Testing Tool Drift: `sim-ui-dump` Contract Is Not Trustworthy Right Now

Before seeded pins, `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` produced useful files but exited nonzero because the proof schema rejected the dump:

```text
proof report contract check failed: /tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json/app: must NOT have additional properties
```

This means the simulator dump producer and `contract/proof/sim-ui-dump.schema.json` have drifted. The dump still wrote:

- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json`
- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.md`

After seeding five pinned rows, a second `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` hung during the current visible screen XCTest path and had to be killed. The lower-level Mobile MCP accessibility dump still worked and captured the pinned state. This is relevant because the formal proof path is currently weak around exactly the UI state under investigation.

## Investigation Log

### 2026-06-02T12:03Z Initial Source Triage

Actions:

- Confirmed active goal and physical iPhone 17 Pro no-touch constraint.
- Searched source for `pin`, `pinned`, `unpin`, `swipeActions`, `contextMenu`, degraded health, and route-health terms.
- Read `DockPinnedViews.swift`, `DockView.swift`, `DockStore.swift`, and `DockCardProjection.swift`.

Learned:

- Pinned rows are implemented as a custom UIKit `UICollectionView` list with trailing swipe actions and long-press reorder.
- Pinned rows call `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update when not actively moving.
- Body rows use a separate SwiftUI offset-based swipe row and are not equivalent to pinned rows.
- Pinned row content intentionally disables the normal context menu.
- Unpin persistence is local metadata; the observed failure is probably before persistence because the action cannot be stably tapped.

### 2026-06-02T12:07Z Relay And Health Evidence

Actions:

- Queried local and home relay health endpoints.
- Opened System Health in the `iPhone 17` simulator through accessibility, not screenshots.
- Opened `Home` host detail inside System Health.
- Read `ThreadCardTable`, `AppConnectivityStore`, `SystemHealthView`, and `SystemHealthProjector`.

Learned:

- Relays were reachable and `/syncz` returned `state=available`.
- The simulator global indicator showed `Online 2/2`, but value `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
- System Health showed every category degraded for the same reason: `Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
- The `Home` host detail said `No route evidence yet.`
- Code confirms route diagnostics are not auto-fetched when System Health opens; the `Run check` button is the fetch path.
- Code confirms global `.partial` falls back to category `.degraded` when a category has no route evidence.

Conclusion:

The broad degraded UI is a client classification bug. A capped Dock row window is being presented as feature degradation across unrelated categories.

### 2026-06-02T12:11Z Simulator Pinned-State Reproduction

Actions:

- Confirmed simulator app data had no existing `thread-metadata.json`.
- Fetched current Dock cards from the relay card stream to avoid guessing metadata keys.
- Seeded five simulator-only local metadata pins using real `hostID/backendSessionID/threadID` keys.
- Relaunched the app with `FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'`.
- Dumped visible simulator accessibility via Mobile MCP against the simulator UDID.

Learned:

- The simulator Dock loaded with `pinned=5`.
- The pinned header displayed `Pinned 5`.
- At least one pinned row was visible and carried accessibility value `Pinned`.
- Pin persistence and projection survived restart.

Conclusion:

The remaining pinned problem is focused on the interaction layer: exposing and tapping `Unpin` on pinned rows.

### 2026-06-02T12:13Z Formal UI Dump Gap

Actions:

- Ran `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` after seeded pins.
- Stopped the dump after it hung.

Learned:

- The first dump before seeded pins already revealed schema drift: top-level `app` exists in produced JSON but is rejected by the proof schema.
- The second dump hung in `CodexDockCurrentUIDumpTests/testDumpsCurrentVisibleScreenOnce`; only config was written under `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T121309Z/`.
- Mobile MCP accessibility dumping still worked.

Conclusion:

Our simulator proof path has blind spots in this class of bug. It can fail schema validation or hang in the precise pinned/high-text accessibility state we need to diagnose.

## Ranked Hypotheses

### H1: Pinned UIKit `reloadData()` closes swipe actions during live updates

Confidence: high after source triage plus simulator pinned-state reproduction; not yet instrumented with a swipe-open timestamp.

Mechanism:

- User swipes a pinned row.
- UIKit opens the trailing `Unpin` action.
- A live Dock update, projection revision, health state update, height measurement callback, or other SwiftUI state change re-runs `updateUIView`.
- `updateUIView` calls `collectionView.reloadData()`.
- UIKit closes the open swipe action.
- User sees the menu pop in and out before it can be tapped.

Why it fits:

- The symptom is instability of the menu, not a failed `Unpin` action after tap.
- It can be worse after startup, when streams/health/status updates are still settling.
- It can be worse with live work happening, because updates keep arriving.
- It is specific to pinned rows because pinned rows use a collection view bridge.

What would prove it:

- Simulator reproduction where opening a pinned-row swipe action followed by a live Dock update or forced render update closes the action.
- Logs/instrumentation showing `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView.updateUIView`/`reloadData()` happens while the swipe action is open.
- A UI dump or XCTest proof showing `Unpin` action appears and disappears across samples without user tapping it.

Current evidence:

- The exact code path calls `collectionView.reloadData()` on every `updateUIView` while not moving.
- The simulator reproduced the same five-pinned startup state.
- The app is live and continuously receiving Dock stream/health changes.
- UIKit list reloads are known to close active cell swipe actions.

This is the most direct explanation for the reported "appears then disappears" menu behavior.

### H2: Long-press reorder recognizer competes with swipe recognizer

Confidence: medium.

Mechanism:

- Pinned rows add a `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` for drag reorder with `minimumPressDuration = 0.35`.
- The recognizer has `cancelsTouchesInView = true`.
- Gesture delegate returns false for simultaneous recognition when either gesture is a long press.
- Slow/hesitant swipes could be interpreted as long press/reorder attempts, canceling the swipe action.

Why it fits:

- User describes inconsistent menu behavior.
- Pinned rows uniquely combine swipe actions and long-press reordering.

What would prove it:

- Simulator reproduction where slow swipes fail but fast swipes work.
- Gesture logs showing long-press began/canceled near failed swipe attempts.

### H3: Hidden pinned rows by filter/scope are being mistaken for stuck pinned rows

Confidence: low-medium.

Mechanism:

- `DockCardProjection` computes `pinnedRows` only from filtered rows.
- `allPinnedRows` includes all pinned rows.
- If filters/scope hide pinned rows, header can show `Pinned X of Y`.

Why it partially fits:

- User had five pinned, then two unpinned, leaving three.
- Existing UI has hidden pinned summary paths.

Why it does not fit well:

- User says the three rows are visible and swipe actions are unstable, not hidden.
- This does not explain the swipe menu appearing and disappearing.

What would prove/disprove it:

- UI dump showing header/title, visible pinned row count, active filters, and actual pinned summary.

### H4: Unpin persistence fails after tap

Confidence: low based on current report.

Mechanism:

- `metadataEngine.setPinned(false, for:)` throws.
- `persistMetadataChange` sets an action error and pinned state remains.

Why it does not fit well:

- User specifically reports not getting a stable unpin menu.
- Need evidence of a tap completing and a persistence error before elevating this.

What would prove it:

- `DockLog` action error or metadata write error after tapping `Unpin`.

### H5: Health categories are degraded because route health is unproven/unknown after restart

Confidence: superseded.

This was the first health hypothesis, but the simulator proved a different specific path. Unknown route evidence is real, but unknown-only diagnostics are not what caused the observed broad degraded labels. The observed labels happened because no route evidence had been loaded into the System Health view, so it fell back from global `.partial`.

### H6: Dock row-window partiality is incorrectly reused as broad service degradation

Confidence: high; reproduced in simulator and confirmed in code.

Mechanism:

- Home relay has more rows than the current Dock stream window limit.
- `ThreadCardTable.hostStatus(...)` returns `.partial(rowCount: 250, message: "Showing 250 of 964")`.
- `AppConnectivityStore.reportDockState` records that as `HostConnectivityPhase.partial("Showing 250 of 964")`.
- Overall connectivity becomes `.partial("Home: Showing 250 of 964")`.
- System Health opens without route diagnostics because `refreshRelayDiagnostics()` only runs from `Run check`.
- `SystemHealthProjector` sees no category route diagnostics and maps global `.partial` to `.degraded` for every category.

Why it fits:

- Simulator exactly displayed this state.
- Host detail exactly showed `No route evidence yet`.
- Every category used the same Dock window message.
- Relay `/syncz` was available and app-critical failures were empty.

What would prove it further:

- A unit test where `SystemHealthProjector.snapshot(hosts: [Home partial window], overallStatus: .partial("Home: Showing 250 of 964"))` with empty `routeDiagnostics` proves every category is currently degraded.
- A corrected test where row-window partiality no longer maps to service degradation.

## Verification Plan

1. Inspect health category mapping in Swift and route-health semantics in relay scripts.
2. Capture current local and home relay `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and `/syncz` payload summaries.
3. Run `rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'` or `FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'` as needed.
4. Use simulator UI dump before and after pinning/unpinning where possible:
   - `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'`
5. Create or use existing UI automation/accessibility path to pin several rows, restart/relaunch the simulator app, and sample pinned-row action visibility.
6. Capture simulator logs:
   - `rtk make sim-logs SIM='iPhone 17'`
7. Update this doc with proved root cause, disproved theories, and fix-ready status only when evidence is strong.

## Fix Plan

<!-- bugs:block:fix_plan -->

Not implemented. Proposed shape for review:

1. Split "Dock data window is partial" from "connectivity/service health is degraded."
   - `Showing 250 of 964` is a Dock data completeness/status message.
   - It should not drive global connectivity or System Health feature degradation by itself.
   - Keep the message visible in Dock where row-window completeness matters.
2. Make System Health route-evidence based.
   - Opening System Health should either fetch route diagnostics automatically or clearly show `Not checked` until the user runs a check.
   - A category should be `Degraded` only for direct failed/degraded/stale evidence in that category, not because Dock has a capped row window.
3. Replace the pinned row interaction path with one stable implementation.
   - Preferred permanent fix: stop using the custom embedded `UICollectionView` for pinned rows if reorder can be achieved with a SwiftUI-native list/stack path, or at least stop unconditional `reloadData()` during normal updates.
   - If keeping UIKit temporarily, update only changed rows with diffable data source or batch updates and never call `reloadData()` while a swipe action is open.
   - Reevaluate the long-press reorder recognizer so it does not cancel swipe actions.
4. Add tests for live-like behavior, not static snapshots only.
   - Pinned row UI test: seed or pin 5 rows, relaunch, open a pinned row swipe action, inject/replay a Dock update, assert `Unpin` remains visible long enough to tap.
   - Health projector test: capped Dock row window does not mark thread detail/archive/voice/diagnostics degraded.
   - System Health UI/accessibility test: with no route evidence, categories show `Not checked` or route-specific healthy/degraded states, not copied Dock window text.
   - Fix `sim-ui-dump` schema drift and add a regression so producer and schema cannot drift.

<!-- /bugs:block:fix_plan -->

## Implementation

<!-- bugs:block:implementation -->

No code changes made in analyze mode.

<!-- /bugs:block:implementation -->

562	    private func rollup(_ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot]) -> AppConnectivityOverallStatus {
563	        guard !hosts.isEmpty else {
564	            return bootstrapStatus ?? .unconfigured("No relay host configured.")
565	        }
566	
567	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
568	            if case .configurationError = $0.phase { return true }
569	            return false
570	        }) {
571	            return .configurationError(status.phase.message)
572	        }
573	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
574	            if case .backgrounded = $0.phase { return true }
575	            return false
576	        }) {
577	            return .backgrounded("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
578	        }
579	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
580	            if case .resuming = $0.phase { return true }
581	            return false
582	        }) {
583	            return .resuming("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
584	        }
585	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
586	            if case .reconnecting = $0.phase { return true }
587	            return false
588	        }) {
589	            return .reconnecting("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
590	        }
591	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
592	            if case .stale = $0.phase { return true }
593	            return false
594	        }) {
595	            return .stale("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
596	        }
597	        let onlineLikeCount = hosts.filter { $0.phase.isOnlineLike }.count
598	        let checkingCount = hosts.filter { status in
599	            if case .checking = status.phase {
600	                return true
601	            }
602	            return false
603	        }.count
604	        if checkingCount == hosts.count {
605	            return .checking(hosts.count == 1 ? hosts[0].phase.message : "Checking \(hosts.count) hosts")
606	        }
607	        if onlineLikeCount > 0, checkingCount > 0 {
608	            return .partial("Online \(onlineLikeCount)/\(hosts.count), checking \(checkingCount)")
609	        }
610	        if onlineLikeCount == hosts.count {
611	            if let partial = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
612	                if case .partial = $0.phase { return true }
613	                return false
614	            }) {
615	                return .partial("\(partial.displayName): \(partial.phase.message)")
616	            }
617	            return .online(hosts.count == 1 ? hosts[0].phase.message : "\(hosts.count) hosts online")
618	        }
619	        if onlineLikeCount > 0 {
620	            let failing = hosts.first { !$0.phase.isOnlineLike } ?? hosts[0]
621	            return .partial("\(failing.displayName): \(failing.phase.message)")
622	        }
623	
624	        if let error = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
625	            if case .error = $0.phase { return true }
626	            return false
627	        }) {
628	            return .error("\(error.displayName): \(error.phase.message)")
629	        }
630	        if let offline = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
631	            if case .offline = $0.phase { return true }
632	            return false
633	        }) {
634	            return .offline("\(offline.displayName): \(offline.phase.message)")
635	        }
636	
637	        return .checking("Waiting for first check")
638	    }

640	    private func priority(for phase: HostConnectivityPhase) -> Int {
641	        switch phase {
642	        case .configurationError:
643	            return 0
644	        case .backgrounded:
645	            return 1
646	        case .resuming:
647	            return 2
648	        case .reconnecting:
649	            return 3
650	        case .stale:
651	            return 4
652	        case .checking:
653	            return 5
654	        case .offline:
655	            return 6
656	        case .error:
657	            return 7
658	        case .partial:
659	            return 8
660	        case .online:
661	            return 9
662	        case .unknown:
663	            return 10
664	        }
665	    }

668	        _ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot],
669	        matching predicate: (HostConnectivitySnapshot) -> Bool
670	    ) -> HostConnectivitySnapshot? {
671	        hosts.first(where: predicate)
672	    }

688	            DockLog.connectivity.info("connectivity host phase host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) endpoint=\(host.endpoint, privacy: .public) phase=\(host.phase.logDescription, privacy: .public) message=\(DockLog.redacted(host.phase.message), privacy: .public)")

250	    private func reload(showLoading: Bool) async {
251	        guard !hosts.isEmpty else {
252	            DockLog.dock.warning("dock reload skipped reason=no_hosts")
253	            return
254	        }
255	        guard !isLoading else {
256	            DockLog.dock.debug("dock reload skipped reason=already_loading")
257	            return
258	        }
259	
260	        let startedAt = Date()
261	        let signpostState = DockSignpost.dock.beginInterval("dock.reload")
262	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock stream reload started hosts=\(self.hosts.count, privacy: .public) show_loading=\(showLoading, privacy: .public)")
263	        isLoading = true
264	        defer {
265	            DockSignpost.dock.endInterval("dock.reload", signpostState)
266	            isLoading = false
267	        }
268	
269	        let hostViewModels = hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init)
270	        if showLoading {
271	            state = .loading(hostViewModels)
272	            screenStore.setLoading(hosts: hostViewModels)
273	            publishConnectivity(for: state)
274	        }
275	
276	        do {
277	            localMetadata = try await metadataEngine.load()
278	            DockLog.persistence.debug("dock metadata loaded entries=\(self.localMetadata.count, privacy: .public)")
279	        } catch {
280	            localMetadata = [:]
281	            await metadataEngine.replace(localMetadata)
282	            DockLog.persistence.warning("dock metadata load failed error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
283	        }
284	
285	        await dataEngine?.updateLocalMetadata(localMetadata)
286	        await dataEngine?.ensureHosts()
287	        await synchronizeStreams()
288	        await migrateMetadataHostAliases()
289	        await publishSnapshot()
290	        if case let .loaded(snapshot) = state {
291	            DockLog.dock.notice("dock stream reload finished hosts=\(self.hosts.count, privacy: .public) rows=\(snapshot.rowCount, privacy: .public) duration_ms=\(DockLog.milliseconds(since: startedAt), privacy: .public)")
292	        }
293	    }

3	public struct SystemHealthProjector: Sendable {
4	    public init() {}
5	
6	    public func snapshot(
7	        hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot],
8	        overallStatus: AppConnectivityOverallStatus
9	    ) -> SystemHealthSnapshot {
10	        SystemHealthSnapshot(
11	            summary: overallStatus,
12	            categories: SystemHealthCategory.allCases.map { category in
13	                SystemHealthCategorySnapshot(
14	                    category: category,
15	                    status: status(for: category, hosts: hosts, overallStatus: overallStatus)
16	                )
17	            },
18	            hosts: hosts
19	        )
20	    }
21	
22	    private func status(
23	        for category: SystemHealthCategory,
24	        hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot],
25	        overallStatus: AppConnectivityOverallStatus
26	    ) -> SystemHealthCategoryStatus {
27	        if hosts.isEmpty {
28	            return .notChecked("No relay host is configured.")
29	        }
30	
31	        let routeNames = routeNames(for: category)
32	        let diagnostics = hosts.flatMap(\.routeDiagnostics).filter { routeNames.contains($0.route) }
33	        if diagnostics.isEmpty {
34	            return fallbackStatus(for: category, overallStatus: overallStatus)
35	        }
36	
37	        if let failed = diagnostics.first(where: { diagnostic in
38	            diagnostic.routeStatus == .failed || diagnostic.routeStatus == .blocked
39	        }) {
40	            return .failed(
41	                failed.statusReasons.first?.message ?? "\(category.title) is failing.",
42	                nextAction: "Run check or open host details."
43	            )
44	        }
45	
46	        if let degraded = diagnostics.first(where: { diagnostic in
47	            diagnostic.routeStatus == .degraded || diagnostic.routeStatus == .partial || diagnostic.routeStatus == .stale
48	        }) {
49	            return .degraded(
50	                degraded.statusReasons.first?.message ?? "\(category.title) has partial or stale evidence.",
51	                nextAction: "Run check or review technical details."
52	            )
53	        }
54	
55	        if diagnostics.contains(where: { $0.routeStatus == .healthy }) {
56	            return .healthy("\(category.title) route evidence is healthy.")
57	        }
58	
59	        return .notChecked("No completed check for \(category.title.lowercased()).")
60	    }
61	
62	    private func fallbackStatus(
63	        for category: SystemHealthCategory,
64	        overallStatus: AppConnectivityOverallStatus
65	    ) -> SystemHealthCategoryStatus {
66	        switch overallStatus {
67	        case .checking, .reconnecting, .resuming:
68	            return .checking("Checking relay health.")
69	        case .online:
70	            switch category {
71	            case .dockFeed:
72	                return .healthy("Dock feed is receiving app evidence.")
73	            case .diagnostics:
74	                return .healthy("Relay process is reachable.")
75	            case .threadDetail, .archive, .voice:
76	                return .notChecked("No recent \(category.title.lowercased()) evidence.")
77	            }
78	        case .partial(let message):
79	            return .degraded(message, nextAction: "Run check or open host details.")
80	        case .offline(let message), .error(let message), .configurationError(let message), .unconfigured(let message):
81	            return .failed(message, nextAction: "Open Relay Settings.")
82	        case .backgrounded(let message):
83	            return .stale(message, nextAction: "Bring the app foreground to refresh.")
84	        case .stale(let message):
85	            return .stale(message, nextAction: "Run check.")
86	        }
87	    }
88	
89	    private func routeNames(for category: SystemHealthCategory) -> Set<String> {
90	        switch category {
91	        case .dockFeed:
92	            return [AppServerMethods.dockSubscribe, AppServerMethods.dockUpdate, AppServerMethods.dockResync]
93	        case .threadDetail:
94	            return [
95	                AppServerMethods.threadDetailSubscribe,
96	                AppServerMethods.threadDetailUpdate,
97	                AppServerMethods.threadDetailResync,
98	            ]
99	        case .archive:
100	            return [
101	                AppServerMethods.archiveSubscribe,
102	                AppServerMethods.archiveUpdate,
103	                AppServerMethods.archiveResync,
104	                AppServerMethods.threadArchive,
105	                AppServerMethods.threadUnarchive
106	            ]
107	        case .voice:
108	            return [
109	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionStart,
110	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionAppend,
111	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionCommit,
112	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionCompleted
113	            ]
114	        case .diagnostics:
115	            return [AppServerMethods.initialize, AppServerMethods.initialized]
116	        }
117	    }
118	}

118	    private struct OperationRecord: Sendable {
119	        var context: AppServerRequestObservabilityContext
120	        var startedAt: Date
121	    }
122	
123	    private let now: @Sendable () -> Date
124	    private let persistenceDirectory: URL?
125	    private let maxOperations: Int
126	    private var operations: [String: OperationRecord] = [:]
127	    private var routeDiagnostics: [String: RouteDiagnosticSnapshot] = [:]
128	
129	    public init(
130	        persistenceDirectory: URL? = ClientObservabilityStore.defaultPersistenceDirectory(),
131	        maxOperations: Int = 200,
132	        now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = Date.init
133	    ) {
134	        self.persistenceDirectory = persistenceDirectory
135	        self.maxOperations = maxOperations
136	        self.now = now
137	    }
138	
139	    public func start(_ context: AppServerRequestObservabilityContext) {
140	        operations[context.operationID] = OperationRecord(context: context, startedAt: now())
141	        trimOperations()
142	    }
143	
144	    public func finish(
145	        _ context: AppServerRequestObservabilityContext,
146	        result: Result<Void, Error>
147	    ) {
148	        let finishedAt = now()
149	        let config = ObservabilityContract.config(for: context.route)
150	        let existing = routeDiagnostics["\(context.configuredHostID)::\(context.route)"]
151	        let snapshot: RouteDiagnosticSnapshot
152	        switch result {
153	        case .success:
154	            snapshot = RouteDiagnosticSnapshot(
155	                configuredHostID: context.configuredHostID,
156	                relayHostID: context.relayHostID,
157	                route: context.route,
158	                operationID: context.operationID,
159	                routeStatus: .healthy,
160	                lastAttemptAt: finishedAt,
161	                lastSuccessAt: finishedAt,
162	                lastFailureAt: existing?.lastFailureAt,
163	                appCritical: config.appCritical
164	            )
165	        case .failure(let error):
166	            snapshot = RouteDiagnosticSnapshot(
167	                configuredHostID: context.configuredHostID,
168	                relayHostID: context.relayHostID,
169	                route: context.route,
170	                operationID: context.operationID,
171	                routeStatus: .failed,
172	                statusReasons: [
173	                    RouteStatusReason(
174	                        code: "failed:last-attempt",
175	                        message: error.localizedDescription,
176	                        actual: failureCategory(for: error).rawValue,
177	                        evidenceIDs: [context.operationID]
178	                    )
179	                ],
180	                lastAttemptAt: finishedAt,
181	                lastSuccessAt: existing?.lastSuccessAt,
182	                lastFailureAt: finishedAt,
183	                appCritical: config.appCritical
184	            )
185	        }
186	        routeDiagnostics[snapshot.id] = snapshot
187	        operations.removeValue(forKey: context.operationID)
188	        persist()
189	    }

192	        route: String,
193	        configuredHostID: String,
194	        relayHostID: String? = nil,
195	        operationID: String? = nil
196	    ) {
197	        let config = ObservabilityContract.config(for: route)
198	        let timestamp = now()
199	        let snapshot = RouteDiagnosticSnapshot(
200	            configuredHostID: configuredHostID,
201	            relayHostID: relayHostID,
202	            route: route,
203	            operationID: operationID,
204	            routeStatus: .healthy,
205	            lastAttemptAt: timestamp,
206	            lastSuccessAt: timestamp,
207	            appCritical: config.appCritical
208	        )

214	        configuredHostID: String,
215	        relayRoutes: [RouteDiagnosticSnapshot]
216	    ) {
217	        for route in relayRoutes {
218	            let snapshot = RouteDiagnosticSnapshot(

220	                relayHostID: route.relayHostID,
221	                route: route.route,
222	                operationID: route.operationID,

237	        routeDiagnostics.values.sorted {
238	            if $0.configuredHostID == $1.configuredHostID {
239	                return $0.route < $1.route
240	            }
241	            return $0.configuredHostID < $1.configuredHostID
242	        }
243	    }

250	        ClientDiagnosticBundle(
251	            schema: "codexdock.appBundle.v1",
252	            createdAt: now(),
253	            appBuild: Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleVersion") as? String ?? "unknown",
254	            hosts: hosts,
255	            routeDiagnostics: snapshots(),
256	            omitted: ["prompts", "transcripts", "audio", "headers", "full-jsonrpc-payloads"]
257	        )
258	    }

260	    private func trimOperations() {
261	        guard operations.count > maxOperations else {
262	            return
263	        }
264	        let extra = operations.count - maxOperations
265	        for key in operations.keys.prefix(extra) {
266	            operations.removeValue(forKey: key)
267	        }
268	    }

270	    private func persist() {
271	        guard let persistenceDirectory else {
272	            return
273	        }
274	        do {
275	            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: persistenceDirectory, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
276	            let bundle = diagnosticBundle(hosts: Array(Set(routeDiagnostics.values.map(\.configuredHostID))).sorted())
277	            let data = try JSONEncoder.diagnostics.encode(bundle)
278	            try data.write(to: persistenceDirectory.appendingPathComponent("client-observability.json"), options: [.atomic])
279	        } catch {
280	            DockLog.connectivity.warning("client observability persistence failed error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
281	        }
282	    }

284	    private func failureCategory(for error: Error) -> ObservabilityFailureCategory {
285	        if let clientError = error as? AppServerClientError {
286	            switch clientError {
287	            case .requestTimedOut:
288	                return .timeout
289	            case .requestCancelled:
290	                return .cancelled
291	            case .server(let object):
292	                if object.code == -32601 {
293	                    return .unsupported
294	                }
295	                if object.code == -32602 {
296	                    return .validation
297	                }
298	                return .relay
299	            case .transport, .disconnected, .notConnected:
300	                return .downstream
301	            default:
302	                return .relay
303	            }
304	        }
305	        return .relay
306	    }

309	        guard let applicationSupport = FileManager.default.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first else {
310	            return nil
311	        }
312	        return applicationSupport
313	            .appendingPathComponent("CodexDock", isDirectory: true)
314	            .appendingPathComponent("Diagnostics", isDirectory: true)
315	    }
316	}

20	# TL;DR
21	
22	## Outcome
23	
24	Codex Dock must show current Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail state through one
25	relay-owned production truth path, and every freshness claim must be proven over
26	time from source change to rendered iPhone UI state.
27	
28	## Problem
29	
30	The app can look connected while the data is stale because liveness,
31	freshness, current-screen proof, relay state, Swift state, and test evidence are
32	not all bound to one contract. Static snapshots and route-health checks can
33	pass while the simulator still shows a stale or wrong Thread view.
34	
35	## Approach
36	
37	Make the relay the only owner of card truth, order, freshness, stream identity,
38	and heartbeat. Make Swift render that contract, reject stale compatible state,
39	rehydrate Thread Detail when relay recovery invalidates continuity, and expose a
40	canonical current-simulator UI dump command for what the app is showing right
41	now. Proof must be retained JSON/Markdown over time, not screenshots,
42	recordings, or one-shot fixtures.
43	
44	## Projection Supersession
45	
46	This live-update plan documents the already-built card-v2 implementation, but
47	the permanent projection identity architecture supersedes it wherever identity,
48	ordering, freshness, cache validity, proof truth, or phone-facing display DTOs
49	are involved.
50	
51	Canonical target:
52	
53	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_THREAD_DETAIL_OUTBOUND_DUPLICATE_ROOT_CAUSE_2026-06-01.md`
54	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md`
55	  `Proposed Projection Identity Contract`
56	
57	After projection cutover, Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail all use projection
58	`rows` keyed by `projectionID` with shared `snapshot` / `upsert` / `delete` /
59	`heartbeat` / `resyncRequired` semantics. The card-v2 `delta`,
60	`stateGeneration`, `baseSeq`, `upsertCards`, `deleteCardIDs`, and
61	`logicalHostID::threadID` vocabulary in this doc is pre-cutover implementation
62	history only. Raw `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, and `thread/resume` are
63	relay-internal adapters or diagnostics, not production display routes.
64	
65	Post-cutover acceptance proof must fetch the relay projection view with the same
66	`viewParamsKey` the simulator UI is rendering, then compare UI accessibility
67	state to that relay view. It must not compare against the full unfiltered ledger
68	or a client-side reconstruction.
69	
70	## Plan
71	
72	Implementation moved depth-first through the real seams: current-simulator UI
73	dump, heartbeat/liveness, Swift stream guards, active Archive stream parity,
74	Thread Detail recovery and full history, relay freshness, proof schemas,
75	proof cadence, and README/runbook alignment. Final simulator evidence is
76	retained at
77	`/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-controlled-matrix-final3-20260601T055358Z/controlled-simulator-matrix.json`.
78	
79	## Non-negotiables
80	
81	- No raw app-server `:4500` phone path for production app behavior.
82	- No local metadata, diagnostics, preview fixtures, or Thread Detail history as
83	  Dock or Archive card truth.
84	- No screenshots or recordings as displayed-state proof.
85	- No skipped UI proof interpreted as a live-update pass.
86	- No runtime fallback or compatibility shim unless this doc explicitly changes
87	  `fallback_policy` and logs the exception.
88	- No side doors kept for tests.

283	# 1) Key Design Considerations (what matters most)
284	
285	## 1.1 Priorities (ranked)
286	
287	1. User-visible correctness: the top Dock row and open Thread view must reflect
288	   the newest provable state or explicitly show why they are stale.
289	2. Single source of truth: card facts and freshness come from relay stream
290	   contracts, not local reconstruction.
291	3. Fail-loud recovery: stale, corrupt, or unproven state must become visible
292	   and trigger rebuild/resync paths.
293	4. Realistic proof: source changes must be observed over time in the simulator
294	   UI and retained as data.
295	5. Small repo-native implementation: extend existing Makefile, Swift tests,
296	   Node tests, contract generation, and UI proof harnesses.
297	
298	## 1.2 Constraints
299	
300	- Mobile build/test/launch commands are Makefile-owned.
301	- Production timeouts, intervals, ports, and caps belong in
302	  `CodexDock/Configuration/CodexDockConstants.swift` or
303	  `scripts/dock-relay-constants.mjs`.
304	- Phone paths must not carry raw bearer tokens or OpenAI keys.
305	- The relay SQLite cache is a projection cache only; Codex/app-server history
306	  remains durable source history.
307	- The current worktree is dirty from adjacent work; this plan must not revert
308	  unrelated edits.
309	
310	## 1.3 Architectural principles (rules we will enforce)
311	
312	- Extend the existing `dock/*` and `archive/*` stream contract instead of adding
313	  a second card-truth API.
314	- Add behavior-level proof at the route/state/UI boundary instead of broad
315	  repository policing.
316	- Keep current-screen inspection canonical and simple: one Makefile target, one
317	  JSON artifact, one short summary.
318	- Use code comments only at sharp contract boundaries such as heartbeat,
319	  generation rejection, and simulator UI dumping.
320	- Prefer hard cutover and deletes over compatibility shims.
321	
322	## 1.4 Known tradeoffs (explicit)
323	
324	- Closing Thread Detail downstream sockets on upstream recovery is blunt, but it
325	  reuses Swift's existing rehydrate path and avoids a half-designed replay
326	  protocol.
327	- Adding proof-result schemas is extra contract work, but it prevents proof
328	  reports from drifting into unauditable JSON blobs.
329	- The simulator current-screen dump is operator evidence, not acceptance proof;
330	  it is intentionally lighter than the full displayed-UI sync proof.
