332	# 2) Problem Statement (existing architecture + why change)
333	
334	## 2.1 What exists today
335	
336	The relay materializes Dock and Archive card projections in SQLite and serves
337	`dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/subscribe`,
338	`archive/update`, and `archive/resync`. Swift consumes those streams through
339	`AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`, applies them in `ThreadCardTable`, and
340	renders through `DockStore`, `ArchiveStore`, and screen stores. Thread Detail
341	loads history with `thread/read`, paged `thread/turns/list`, then
342	`thread/resume`.
343	
344	The repo also has relay scenario proof, controlled simulator fixture proof, and
345	XCTest accessibility sampling through `CodexDockDisplayedSyncProofTests`.
346	
347	## 2.2 Original broken / missing behavior (concrete)
348	
349	- Relay schema and Swift understand `kind:"heartbeat"`, but production relay
350	  subscriptions do not emit periodic heartbeat updates.
351	- Swift applies compatible snapshots without rejecting older
352	  `stateGeneration` values.
353	- Relay upstream Thread Detail recovery can succeed invisibly, leaving the phone
354	  connected without forcing a rehydrate.
355	- `ThreadTurnsListParams` has no `itemsView`, so the detail path cannot require
356	  `itemsView:"full"` even though the proof script can.
357	- Live endpoint/source failures can be hidden by history completeness instead
358	  of failing the visible freshness state closed.
359	- Archive mutation scheduling exists but Archive convergence is not yet a
360	  first-class invariant equal to Dock convergence.
361	- Proof harnesses exist but are not fully schema-guarded, scheduled, or
362	  required for update-path changes.
363	- There is no repo-owned lightweight command to dump the current simulator Dock
364	  or Thread visual state on demand.
365	
366	## 2.3 Current implementation state
367	
368	The implemented architecture closes the original gaps:
369	
370	- Production relay subscriptions emit heartbeat updates for Dock and Archive.
371	- Swift stream application rejects stale compatible generations and uses one
372	  shared stream lifecycle for Dock and active Archive.
373	- Archive Cleanup no longer owns a cleanup-only Dock snapshot side door.
374	- Thread Detail requests full turn items on the visible detail path and
375	  rehydrates after relay upstream recovery closes the downstream phone socket.
376	- Live-source refresh failures make relay freshness stale/partial instead of
377	  publishing falsely fresh state.
378	- Proof reports are schema-checked and reject raw app-server `:4500` evidence,
379	  scripted stream side doors, mismatched proof run IDs, and missing route
380	  evidence.
381	- `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` dumps the current simulator screen as
382	  accessibility JSON/Markdown without relaunching, navigating, seeding, or
383	  taking screenshots.
384	- `rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof SIM='iPhone 17'` proves over-time
385	  convergence from controlled relay truth to visible simulator UI, including
386	  visible ordering.
387	
388	## 2.4 Constraints implied by the problem
389	
390	The fix cannot be a single Swift UI patch. It must bind the relay data contract,
391	Swift state model, Thread Detail session model, proof artifacts, and Makefile
392	entrypoints so a stale simulator cannot look "green" because only static or
393	diagnostic checks ran.

801	## 5.4 Invariants and boundaries
802	
803	- Relay owns Dock and Archive card truth. Swift can filter, group, pin, label,
804	  and render, but it cannot create/order/freshen card truth from another route.
805	- Archive uses the same generated card stream contract as Dock and must not
806	  silently drift in freshness semantics. The active Archive screen uses the
807	  same stream liveness model as Dock; snapshot-only Archive reads are not a
808	  user-visible freshness path.
809	- Archive Cleanup is product UI, not a test helper. This plan keeps it and
810	  migrates it to the same stream-backed card state; it cannot keep Dock
811	  snapshot loading as a cleanup-only shortcut.
812	- Stream corruption or stale generation causes resync/reconnect/fail-visible,
813	  not silent accept.
814	- Thread Detail history completeness is explicit: `itemsView:"full"` for
815	  detail, not for cheap card-order proof.
816	- Dock and Thread Detail displayed ordering is proof-critical. Accessibility
817	  samples preserve top-to-bottom frame order; sorting by identifier is forbidden
818	  because it can hide reversed/newest-first bugs.
819	- The simulator dump command is an operator inspection tool. It cannot satisfy
820	  over-time proof gates by itself.
821	- No compatibility shim is approved. `fallback_policy` remains `forbidden`.

1	# Codex Dock Protocol And Update Architecture Reference
2	
3	Date: 2026-05-31
4	
5	Status: reference plus audit. This document describes the intended architecture,
6	the real update paths in the current repo, the app-server assumptions the relay
7	depends on, and the stale-data failure modes we found while auditing. It does
8	not implement fixes.
9	
10	Current UX intention:
11	[CODEX_DOCK_USER_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md](CODEX_DOCK_USER_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md),
12	[CODEX_DOCK_TRUSTWORTHY_LIVE_WINDOW_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md](CODEX_DOCK_TRUSTWORTHY_LIVE_WINDOW_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md)
13	and
14	[CODEX_DOCK_LIVE_TRUTH_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md](CODEX_DOCK_LIVE_TRUTH_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md).
15	
16	## Bottom Line
17	
18	Codex Dock has two different update systems:
19	
20	1. Dock and Archive cards are relay-owned streams. The relay polls and
21	   reconciles Codex app-server state into SQLite, then sends `dock/update` or
22	   `archive/update` to subscribed clients.
23	2. Thread Detail is a live forwarded session. The client reads historical turns,
24	   then asks the relay to `thread/resume`; the relay binds that phone WebSocket
25	   to an upstream app-server session and forwards live notifications and server
26	   requests.
27	
28	The current test suite is strong at proving that Swift can apply pre-made
29	snapshots, deltas, and live notifications. It is weaker at proving that real
30	Codex work continues flowing from app-server to relay to phone over time. That
31	gap explains how the app can look connected while a thread or Dock list stops
32	updating.
33	
34	The highest-signal stale-data failures found in this audit are:
35	
36	- Dock can reconnect its WebSocket and re-run `initialize` without re-running
37	  `dock/subscribe`; the stream can look alive but stop receiving card updates.
38	- Thread Detail can miss history after relay-side upstream recovery because the
39	  relay may recover its Mac-side `thread/resume` session without closing the
40	  phone WebSocket; Swift only rehydrates detail when it observes reconnect,
41	  foreground resume, or stream end.
42	- Route health is not data freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`,
43	  `/metricsz`, and `/syncz` can look healthy while cards are stale, partial, or
44	  no longer receiving updates.
45	- Relay subscribe-time buffering protects one race: the relay subscribes before
46	  reading the initial snapshot and buffers newer updates until the snapshot is
47	  returned. That does not protect reconnects that never re-send
48	  `dock/subscribe`.
49	- Most regular tests use fakes or scripted streams. Those tests prove client
50	  merge/render behavior, not the full real app-server -> relay -> iPhone update
51	  path.
52	
53	## Source Audit Inputs
54	
55	This writeup combines parent-agent code reads with six parallel read-only
56	audits covering app-server assumptions, relay state, Swift streams, Thread
57	Detail, tests, and reconnect/freshness failure modes. The parallel outputs were
58	used as evidence inputs; the file paths and code anchors below are the durable
59	reference.
60	
61	## Vocabulary
62	
63	- App-server: the raw Codex local JSON-RPC server, normally on
64	  `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`.
65	- Relay: the Dock relay process, normally on `:4510`. It owns the raw
66	  app-server bearer token and exposes the phone-safe Dock protocol.
67	- Client: the Swift iOS app.
68	- Downstream: relay -> phone/client.
69	- Upstream: relay -> raw Codex app-server.
70	- Snapshot: a full replacement card payload.
71	- Delta: an incremental card payload.
72	- Heartbeat: a stream payload kind Swift can accept, intended to update
73	  freshness without changing rows.
74	- Rehydrate: Thread Detail's full historical refresh:
75	  `thread/read includeTurns:false`, all pages of `thread/turns/list`, then
76	  `thread/resume excludeTurns:true`.
77	- Freshness: whether the relay believes card facts are current.
78	- Completeness: whether the relay believes it has the full relevant set/window.
79	- Live session: a `thread/resume` connection that can forward notifications,
80	  server requests, and turn commands.
81	
82	## Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules
83	
84	1. The phone normally talks to the relay on `:4510`, not directly to raw
85	   app-server on `:4500`.
86	2. Dock Home card truth comes from relay `dock/*` methods, not raw
87	   `thread/list`.
88	3. Archive card truth comes from relay `archive/*` methods.
89	4. Current legacy Thread Detail history comes from
90	   `thread/read includeTurns:false` plus paged `thread/turns/list`, with
91	   `thread/resume excludeTurns:true` as the live session and compact metadata
92	   path. After the proposed projection cutover, the relay may still use those
93	   raw routes internally, but phone display truth must come from
94	   `thread/detail/*`.
95	5. The relay, not Swift, owns card recency. Pre-cutover Swift renders relay
96	   `orderKey`; projection cutover Swift renders relay `displayOrderKey`. Swift
97	   must not rebuild card recency from local timestamps.
98	6. `thread/list` order is not a client-visible ordering contract. The relay must
99	   prove card activity with `thread/turns/list` before exposing fresh card
100	   order.
101	7. Route health is not freshness. A route can answer and still return stale or
102	   partial data.
103	8. Local client metadata can decorate rows and pin rows, but it must not create
104	   production thread rows or override projection `displayOrderKey` after
105	   cutover.
106	9. Human-started filtering is relay-owned. After projection cutover, filters
107	   that change visible membership are `viewParams` with a `viewParamsKey`;
108	   Swift's defensive second filter is an invalid-data guard only.
109	10. Any reconnect that changes stream/session identity must force the missing
110	    state to be rebuilt, not merely reconnect a socket.
111	11. A normal phone host config must identify relay hosts only. Saved app configs
112	    are a `hosts` list, and Swift rejects raw app-server port `4500` for normal
113	    app endpoints.
114	
115	## Protocol Surface
116	
117	Swift method constants live in `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerMethods.swift`.
118	The relay dispatcher that decides what the phone can call lives in
119	`scripts/dock-relay.mjs`.
120	
121	## Proposed Projection Identity Contract
122	
123	Status: proposed permanent projection contract, not implemented yet. The
124	rationale and root-cause audit live in
125	`docs/CODEX_DOCK_THREAD_DETAIL_OUTBOUND_DUPLICATE_ROOT_CAUSE_2026-06-01.md`.
126	
127	Projection supersession rule: after projection cutover, the sections below that
128	describe card-v2 `delta`, `stateGeneration`, `logicalHostID::threadID`,
129	`upsertCards`, `deleteCardIDs`, or raw Thread Detail display routes are
130	pre-cutover implementation history only. They are not co-equal display
131	contracts and cannot be used as production identity, ordering, or freshness
132	truth.
133	
134	The permanent display source for Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail should be
135	relay-owned projection rows, not raw Codex JSON parsed independently by Swift
136	and proof scripts. Thread Detail is the first urgent cutover, but it must use
137	the same projection identity grammar as Dock and Archive.
138	
139	### Shared Projection Identity Envelope
140	
141	Every user-visible production row/card is a relay projection row. The shared
142	envelope is:
143	
144	```json
145	{
146	  "schemaVersion": 1,
147	  "identityVersion": 1,
148	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
149	  "view": "thread.detail",
150	  "threadID": "019e...",
151	  "projectionID": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1/row:userMessage",
152	  "sourceRef": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1",
153	  "rowRole": "userMessage",
154	  "revision": 7,
155	  "displayOrderKey": "9998239345599999|0000000000|9999999999|9999999999|...",
156	  "freshness": {
157	    "state": "fresh",
158	    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
159	  },
160	  "payload": {}
161	}
162	```
163	
164	Required shared fields:
165	
166	| Field | Meaning |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| `schemaVersion` | Projection DTO shape version. |
169	| `identityVersion` | Projection identity algorithm version. |
170	| `sourceHostID` | Stable Codex source identity; never derived from phone saved host config. |
171	| `view` | `dock`, `archive`, `archive.cleanup`, `host.registry`, or `thread.detail`. |
172	| `threadID` | Raw Codex thread ID when the row belongs to one thread. |
173	| `projectionID` | Stable visible row/card identity, generated only by the relay projection normalizer. |
174	| `sourceRef` | Stable raw Codex fact identity used to derive `projectionID`. |
175	| `rowRole` | Semantic visible role, such as `threadCard`, `userMessage`, `request`, or `system`. |
176	| `revision` | Content revision for the same `projectionID`; it is not identity. |
177	| `displayOrderKey` | Opaque relay-owned ascending sort key. |
178	| `freshness` | Data freshness for this projection row or view. |
179	| `payload` | Typed row payload for the specific view. |
180	
181	Projection IDs include `sourceHostID`:
182	
183	```text
184	host:<sourceHostID>/row:host
185	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
186	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/row:<rowRole>
187	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/request:<requestID>/row:request
188	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/system:<systemEventKind>/<sourceSequenceOrTimestamp>
189	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/diagnostic:<stableHash>/row:unknown
190	```
191	
192	Dock and Archive use the same thread-card projection ID:
193	
194	```text
195	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
196	```
197	
198	`view: "dock"` and `view: "archive"` scope where that card is delivered.
199	Archive state is payload state, not a separate identity namespace. The
200	Dock/Archive card `sourceRef` is:
201	
202	```text
203	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>
204	```
205	
206	The current Dock contract has `logicalHostID`. In the post-cutover projection
207	contract, `logicalHostID` is a legacy/transition alias for `sourceHostID`.
208	If a legacy Dock payload still carries both names, they must map one-to-one.
209	If they disagree, the relay must emit a diagnostic or `resyncRequired`; Swift
210	must not pick one locally.
211	
212	`projectionID` is the only production visible identity field. Older local names
213	such as `eventID` are historical aliases from the pre-projection Thread Detail
214	plan and must not remain as separate wire identity fields after cutover.
215	
216	### Host Projection Rows
217	
218	`host:<sourceHostID>/row:host` is the projection identity for a Codex source
219	host. Host rows carry labels and connectivity summaries; they do not define a
220	second host identity namespace.
221	
222	Host row payload:
223	
224	```json
225	{
226	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
227	  "displayName": "Amir M5",
228	  "endpointLabels": ["amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510"],
229	  "connectivityState": "online",
230	  "lastContactAt": "2026-06-01T19:50:00.000Z"
231	}
232	```
233	
234	Rules:
235	
236	- host rows are keyed only by `sourceHostID`;
237	- endpoint, Bonjour, LAN, Tailscale, and saved-phone labels are payload labels,
238	  never identity;
239	- phone saved host configs are bootstrap connection records only. They may have
240	  local config IDs for settings UI, but those IDs never appear in
241	  `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `displayOrderKey`, or proof
242	  witnesses;
243	- thread-card rows reference the host row through `sourceHostID`;
244	- host row ordering is stable label order unless a future host view defines a
245	  relay-owned `displayOrderKey`.
246	
247	Host Registry routes use the same projection grammar:
248	
249	- `host/registry/read`
250	- `host/registry/subscribe`
251	- `host/registry/update`
252	- `host/registry/resync`
253	
254	`HostRegistrySnapshotDTO` and `HostRegistryUpdateDTO` are shared
255	snapshot/update envelopes with `view: "host.registry"` and host-row payloads.
256	If the app shows configured endpoints before a relay connection exists, that is
257	settings UI backed by phone config, not a projection view and not evidence of
258	Codex source identity. Once connected, user-visible Codex source identity,
259	labels, connectivity summaries, and proof state come from host projection rows.
260	
261	### `sourceHostID` Derivation
262	
263	The relay derives `sourceHostID` with this ordered rule:
264	
265	1. Use non-empty `CODEX_DOCK_REAL_HOST_ID` from relay-side configuration.
266	2. Else use the persisted value in `.codex-dock/source-host-id`.
267	3. Else create `.codex-dock/source-host-id` once as
268	   `local-<sha256(platform + user + CODEX_HOME + historyUrl)[0..12]>`.
269	
270	Validation:
271	
272	- The value must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}`.
273	- Endpoint hostnames, Bonjour names, LAN IPs, Tailscale names, saved phone host
274	  config, WebSocket connection IDs, and relay process IDs are not
275	  `sourceHostID`.
276	- Phone saved host config IDs must not appear in `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`,
277	  `projectionID`, `displayOrderKey`, or proof witnesses.
278	- `CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_INSTANCE_ID` is process/session identity only. It must not
279	  be used in `projectionID`.
280	- Test fixtures may set explicit `sourceHostID` values, but they must still use
281	  the same projection ID grammar.
282	
283	This makes identity stable across endpoint relabeling while still allowing
284	separate Mac/home Codex sources to stay distinct.
285	
286	### Single Projection Engine Module
287	
288	The relay has one production projection engine module:
289	
290	```text
291	scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs
292	```
293	
294	That module, or its owned package directory, is the only production place where
295	helpers named like `projectionIDFor*`, `sourceRefFor*`, row-role mappers,
296	`displayOrderKeyFor*`, or projection-engine version constants may live. Thread
297	Detail ledger code, Dock state code, Archive state code, Host Registry code,
298	Archive Cleanup code, and proof fixtures may call the engine; they must not
299	fork visible identity or ordering logic.
300	
301	Tests may import the pure engine for unit coverage. Acceptance proof may not
302	use that import as its expected-ID oracle. Acceptance proof reads IDs from
303	emitted projection envelopes only.
304	
305	### Shared Projection Snapshot And Update Grammar
306	
307	Each display route emits one shared stream grammar:
308	
309	```json
310	{
311	  "schemaVersion": 1,
312	  "identityVersion": 1,
313	  "projectionEngineVersion": 1,
314	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
315	  "view": "thread.detail",
316	  "threadID": "019e...",
317	  "epoch": "projection-...",
318	  "seq": 42,
319	  "scope": "thread",
320	  "complete": true,
321	  "freshness": {
322	    "state": "fresh",
323	    "asOf": "2026-06-01T18:00:00.000Z",
324	    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
325	  },
326	  "rows": []
327	}
328	```
329	
330	Updates are only:
331	
332	- `snapshot`: replace the declared scope.
333	- `upsert`: insert or replace rows by `projectionID`.
334	- `delete`: remove rows by `projectionID`.
335	- `heartbeat`: prove stream continuity without mutating rows.
336	- `resyncRequired`: declare continuity broken and require a replacement
337	  snapshot.
338	
339	Every update carries `epoch` and monotonic `seq`. Swift applies only the active
340	epoch and increasing sequence. `seq` is the canonical wire field; do not add a
341	parallel `sequence` field for projection streams. Sequence gaps, missing
342	epochs, missing `projectionEngineVersion`, or schema/identity/engine version
343	mismatches mark the view stale until resync succeeds.
344	
345	Every projection snapshot and update envelope carries
346	`projectionEngineVersion`. Swift stores the active engine version with the
347	active epoch. An update with a different `projectionEngineVersion` inside the
348	same epoch is invalid; the client rejects it, marks the view stale, and requests
349	the matching resync route. A new engine version is accepted only through a
350	replacement snapshot with a new epoch.
351	
352	Route-specific notification methods carry this same update grammar:
353	
354	| View | Subscribe/read routes | Passive update notification | Resync route |
355	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
356	| Dock | `dock/subscribe` | `dock/update` | `dock/resync` |
357	| Archive | `archive/subscribe` | `archive/update` | `archive/resync` |
358	| Archive Cleanup | `archive/cleanup/read`, `archive/cleanup/subscribe` | `archive/cleanup/update` | `archive/cleanup/resync` |
359	| Host Registry | `host/registry/read`, `host/registry/subscribe` | `host/registry/update` | `host/registry/resync` |
360	| Thread Detail | `thread/detail/read`, `thread/detail/subscribe` | `thread/detail/update` | `thread/detail/resync` |
361	
362	The notification method name is transport routing only. Identity, ordering,
363	freshness, epoch, and sequence semantics come from the shared projection
364	payload, not from view-specific client code.
365	
366	`heartbeat` updates carry `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `identityVersion`,
367	`projectionEngineVersion`, `sourceHostID`, `view`, `threadID` when scoped to
368	one thread, `epoch`, `seq`, and `freshness`. They carry no `rows`,
369	`projectionIDs`, or payload
370	mutation. A heartbeat proves stream continuity only; it never marks failed data
371	fresh.
372	
373	### Cross-View Scope And Snapshot Authority
374	
375	Accepted projection scopes:
376	
377	| View | Scope | Snapshot authority |
378	| --- | --- | --- |
379	| `dock` | `view` | Complete active Dock view for one `viewParamsKey`; absent rows are deleted. |
380	| `archive` | `view` | Complete Archive view for one `viewParamsKey`; absent rows are deleted. |
381	| `archive.cleanup` | `view` | Complete Archive Cleanup candidate view for one `viewParamsKey`; absent rows are deleted. |
382	| `dock` | `host` | Complete active Dock view for one `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey`. |
383	| `archive` | `host` | Complete Archive view for one `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey`. |
384	| `archive.cleanup` | `host` | Complete cleanup candidate view for one `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey`. |
385	| `dock` / `archive` / `archive.cleanup` | `window` | Bounded `displayOrderKey` range; only rows inside the declared range are replaced. |
386	| `host.registry` | `view` | Complete host registry for one `viewParamsKey`; absent host rows are deleted. |
387	| `thread.detail` | `thread` | Complete detail view for one `threadID` and `viewParamsKey`. |
388	| `thread.detail` | `window` | Bounded detail `displayOrderKey` range for one thread. |
389	
390	Dock and Archive stream envelopes omit `threadID` unless the update is
391	explicitly scoped to one thread. Card rows carry thread identity in the row
392	envelope when present and always in the typed payload. Clients determine
393	snapshot authority from `view`, `scope`, `sourceHostID`, `viewParamsKey`, and
394	window bounds, not by guessing from row IDs.
395	
396	For every view, `snapshot` replaces only its declared scope, `upsert` replaces
397	exact `projectionID`s, `delete` removes exact `projectionID`s, `heartbeat`
398	proves continuity only, and `resyncRequired` makes the active view stale until
399	the matching resync route returns a replacement snapshot.

559	### Projection Cache Version And Contract Gate
560	
561	The relay SQLite cache is a materialized projection, not a source of truth.
562	Every stored projection row is valid only for this cache version:
563	
564	```text
565	schemaVersion + identityVersion + projectionEngineVersion + sourceHostID
566	```
567	
568	If any part changes, rows for that host/view are invalid until rebuilt from raw
569	Codex state. The relay may keep old rows visible only as explicitly stale rows;
570	it must not serve them as fresh under a new identity contract.
571	
572	The protocol contract source is a schema/generator package:
573	
574	- one schema source for the shared projection envelope.
575	- typed payload schemas for Dock/Archive cards and Thread Detail rows.
576	- one accepted wire shape: projection envelope plus nested typed `payload`.
577	- `viewParams` and `viewParamsKey` schema for filtered projection views.
578	- generated or schema-checked Swift DTOs.
579	- Node validation for emitted projection snapshots/updates in tests.
580	- fixture corpus generated from the relay projection normalizer and consumed by
581	  Swift tests.
582	
583	Normative package shape:
584	
585	```text
586	contract/projection/projection-envelope.schema.json
587	contract/projection/projection-snapshot.schema.json
588	contract/projection/projection-update.schema.json
589	contract/projection/payloads/dock-thread-card.schema.json
590	contract/projection/payloads/thread-detail-row.schema.json
591	contract/projection/payloads/host-row.schema.json
592	contract/projection/fixtures/*.json
593	scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs
594	scripts/generate-projection-contract.mjs
595	scripts/check-projection-contract.mjs
596	CodexDock/AppServer/ProjectionDTO.swift
597	```
598	
599	The existing `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` becomes card-v2
600	history after cutover. It is not a co-equal phone-facing display schema.
601	
602	This is a contract gate, not a linter. If identity version, route grammar, enum
603	vocabulary, payload shape, or projection row fields change, Node and Swift tests
604	must fail until the single source and fixtures move together.
605	
606	`revision`, `schemaVersion`, `identityVersion`, and
607	`projectionEngineVersion` are separate:
608	
609	| Field | Bump when |
610	| --- | --- |
611	| `revision` | Content, freshness, render state, request status, or payload changes for the same `projectionID`. |
612	| `schemaVersion` | Projection wire shape changes. |
613	| `identityVersion` | `sourceRef` or `projectionID` rules change. |
614	| `projectionEngineVersion` | Projection membership, order, freshness, row roles, view params, or payload interpretation changes without a wire-shape or ID-grammar change. |
615	
616	`revision` is monotonic per `projectionID` inside one cache contract. Cache
617	validity uses
618	`schemaVersion + identityVersion + projectionEngineVersion + sourceHostID`, not
619	`revision`.
620	
621	For a given `projectionID`, these envelope fields are immutable inside one
622	identity version:
623	
624	- `sourceHostID`
625	- `sourceRef`
626	- `rowRole`
627	- `threadID` when present
628	- `view`
629	- `schemaVersion`
630	- `identityVersion`
631	
632	If an `upsert` repeats a `projectionID` with any of those fields changed, the
633	client rejects the update, marks the view stale, and requests resync. If an
634	`upsert` regresses `revision` inside the same epoch, the client rejects it as
635	stale or requests resync. If the same `revision` carries different payload
636	content, the client treats it as a projection contract violation and requests
637	resync.
638	
639	`epoch` is a relay-generated stream generation identifier. It is unique within
640	`sourceHostID + view + scope + viewParamsKey` and is created by the relay when a
641	projection stream starts, resyncs after stale state, changes
642	`identityVersion`, changes `projectionEngineVersion`, or detects unrecoverable
643	sequence/source loss. A new `epoch` is valid only when delivered with a
644	replacement snapshot. Updates cannot silently hop epochs.
645	
646	`sourceWatermark` is upstream freshness evidence, not row identity. It records
647	the raw Codex history/live point the relay has normalized into the projection
648	ledger. Swift may display or log it as freshness context, but it cannot use it
649	to create, sort, dedupe, or delete rows. If the relay cannot prove a watermark
650	is still compatible with the current projection cache contract, the affected
651	view is stale until resync.
652	
653	### Projection Identity Laws
654	
655	1. No production visible row/card ID may be generated from body text, timestamp,
656	   local UI state, Swift object lifetime, raw WebSocket request ID alone,
657	   `UUID()`, or `crypto.randomUUID()`.
658	2. A supported raw Codex item without enough identity does not become a normal
659	   message/card row. It becomes a stable diagnostic row or a `resyncRequired`
660	   update.
661	3. Live, history, reconnect, canonical reread, server request, request
662	   resolution, cache rebuild, and proof paths all call the same relay projection
663	   normalizer.
664	4. Streaming and settled forms of one Codex item share one `projectionID`.
665	5. Request controls are attached to the same `projectionID` as their visible
666	   row. `requestID` is only the response-routing key.
667	6. Sorting is by relay `displayOrderKey` only.
668	7. Local metadata can decorate projection rows, but it cannot create fresh
669	   production rows or override projection identity/order/freshness.
670	8. Diagnostics and health routes can explain state, but cannot be accepted as
671	   data truth for the UI.
672	9. Test fixtures must use projection DTOs or the relay projection normalizer.
673	10. Proof scripts must compare UI state against relay projection snapshots or
674	    updates, not against an independent reconstruction of raw Codex truth.
675	11. Filters are projection view parameters. Every filtered view has a
676	    `viewParamsKey`, and proof compares UI only to the relay projection view
677	    with the same key.
678	12. Pin and local metadata can decorate existing projection rows, or request a
679	    future relay-owned pinned projection view with explicit `viewParamsKey`.
680	    Swift cannot use local pin state to create a second row order, second
681	    membership set, or alternate cache of projection rows.
682	
683	### Projection Witness Plane
684	
685	Acceptance proof compares simulator accessibility state to a retained witness
686	of relay-emitted projection snapshots and updates from the system under test.
687	
688	Required capture mechanism:
689	
690	- primary path: the proof harness attaches a projection witness recorder to the
691	  actual downstream JSON-RPC projection stream for the simulator app session
692	  before opening the UI; or
693	- the proof harness reads a loopback-only relay diagnostic export, for example
694	  `projection/witness/read`, for the exact `sourceHostID`, `view`, `scope`,
695	  `threadID`, `viewParamsKey`, and `epoch` under test.
696	
697	The diagnostic export is not a display route. It may export only projection
698	envelopes already emitted by the relay projection engine for that session. It
699	must not compute expected IDs from fixture input.
700	
701	`projection/witness/read` is acceptable only if it returns byte-for-byte
702	equivalent projection envelopes retained from the downstream emitter or a
703	retained emitter log. It must not rebuild expected rows from SQLite, raw Codex
704	payloads, fixture JSON, or helper imports at proof time. If downstream capture
705	and diagnostic export disagree, downstream capture wins and the run fails.
706	
707	Allowed witness sources:
708	
709	- the same downstream WebSocket projection snapshots/updates delivered to the
710	  simulator app;
711	- a relay debug export of the active projection ledger for the exact
712	  `sourceHostID`, `view`, `scope`, `threadID`, and `viewParamsKey`;
713	- structured relay logs that retain the emitted projection envelope while
714	  redacting prompt/body text where required.
715	
716	Forbidden witness sources:
717	
718	- fixture code that calls projection helper functions to construct expected
719	  IDs beside the relay;
720	- raw `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, or `thread/resume` truth rebuilt into
721	  expected UI IDs;
722	- `expectedMessageEventIDs`;
723	- `expectedMessageProjectionIDs` unless populated directly from the retained
724	  projection witness stream.
725	- fixture imports of `projectionIDForItem`, `projectionIDForRequest`, or any
726	  equivalent helper to populate acceptance expected IDs.
727	
728	Proof records must name the witness:
729	
730	```json
731	{
732	  "projectionWitness": {
733	    "source": "downstream-projection-stream",
734	    "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
735	    "view": "thread.detail",
736	    "scope": "thread",
737	    "threadID": "019e...",
738	    "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",
739	    "epoch": "projection-...",
740	    "lastSeq": 42,
741	    "projectionIDs": []
742	  }
743	}
744	```
745	
746	Loopback-only witness export contract:
747	
748	`projection/witness/read` request:
749	
750	```json

752	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
753	  "view": "thread.detail",
754	  "scope": "thread",
755	  "threadID": "019e...",
756	  "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",
757	  "epoch": "projection-...",
758	  "fromSeq": 1,
759	  "throughSeq": null
760	}
761	```
762	
763	Response:
764	
765	```json

767	  "source": "retained-downstream-emitter-log",
768	  "byteEquivalentToDownstream": true,
769	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
770	  "view": "thread.detail",
771	  "scope": "thread",
772	  "threadID": "019e...",
773	  "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",

781	Rules:
782	
783	- `projection/witness/read` is not in the phone production display allow-list.
784	- It is loopback/local-test only and must fail closed outside test/diagnostic
785	  configuration.
786	- `envelopes` are retained emitted projection snapshots/updates, not
787	  recomputed projections.
788	- `byteEquivalentToDownstream` must be `true`; otherwise proof cannot use this
789	  route as witness evidence.
790	- `projectionIDs` are derived from `envelopes` by reading emitted row IDs only.

792	### Command And Pending Row Rule
793	
794	Mutation routes such as `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, `turn/interrupt`,
795	`thread/archive`, `thread/unarchive`, and server-request responses are commands.
796	They are not display-truth routes.
797	
798	Projection v1 intentionally does not include Swift-created optimistic display
799	rows. If the product later chooses optimistic rows, they must be relay-owned and
800	specified as a contract extension before implementation:
801	
802	```text
803	clientMutationID -> relay pending projection row -> atomic supersession to canonical sourceRef/projectionID
804	```
805	
806	That extension must define an atomic supersession update or an equivalent
807	snapshot replacement. Swift must never create a production visible pending row
808	from local text, local timestamps, or local UUIDs.
809	
810	If optimistic rows are added, the contract must specify `clientMutationID`, the
811	relay-created pending `projectionID`, the supersession/replacement operation,
812	proof that pending and canonical rows never render together, and cache rules
813	for pending rows on reconnect, failed send, and relay restart.
814	
815	Proposed downstream display routes:
816	
817	- `thread/detail/read`
818	- `thread/detail/subscribe`
819	- `thread/detail/update`
820	- `thread/detail/resync`
821	
822	Request params:
823	
824	```json
825	{
826	  "threadId": "019e...",
827	  "window": {
828	    "offset": 0,
829	    "limit": 250,
830	    "afterDisplayOrderKey": null
831	  }
832	}
833	```
834	
835	`thread/detail/read` returns one `ThreadDetailSnapshotDTO`.
836	`thread/detail/subscribe` accepts the same params, returns an initial
837	`ThreadDetailSnapshotDTO`, then emits JSON-RPC notifications with method
838	`thread/detail/update` and params shaped as `ThreadDetailUpdateDTO`.
839	`thread/detail/update` is passive; the phone never calls it as a request.
840	`thread/detail/resync` accepts the same params plus optional `epoch` and
841	`reason` fields, and returns a replacement `ThreadDetailSnapshotDTO`.
842	
843	`thread/detail/subscribe` also establishes the relay-side thread binding for
844	`turn/start`, `turn/steer`, and `turn/interrupt` on that downstream connection.
845	Internally, the relay may open or maintain upstream `thread/resume
846	excludeTurns:true`, but raw notifications from that upstream session are
847	normalized into projection updates before reaching Swift display state.
848	
849	Existing raw `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, and `thread/resume` may remain
850	relay internals and command/session tools, but they must not be accepted as
851	production Thread Detail display proof after this contract is implemented.

911	### Thread Detail View Params
912	
913	`thread/detail/read`, `thread/detail/subscribe`, and `thread/detail/resync` use
914	the same `viewParams` shape when the visible Thread Detail view is filtered:
915	
916	```json
917	{

919	  "viewParams": {
920	    "visibility": "all",
921	    "rowRoles": null,
922	    "search": "",
923	    "includeDiagnostics": true,
924	    "sort": "displayOrderKeyAscending"
925	  }
926	}
927	```
928	
929	The relay echoes `viewParamsKey` on every snapshot and update. `viewParamsKey`
930	is stable-key-order JSON over `viewParams`, hashed as `sha256:<hex>`. Swift
931	rejects updates whose `viewParamsKey` does not match the active view.
932	
933	Defaults:
934	
935	- `visibility: "all"`; no hidden default message-only filter.
936	- `rowRoles: null`; non-empty arrays are positive include filters.
937	- `search: ""`; non-empty search is part of the relay projection view, not a
938	  local proof oracle.
939	- `includeDiagnostics: true` in development proof.
940	- `sort: "displayOrderKeyAscending"`; no other v1 sort is accepted.

1006	| `projectionEngineVersion` | Projection engine behavior version used for membership, order, freshness, row roles, view params, and payload interpretation. |
1007	| `sourceHostID` | Stable Codex source host identity used in every `projectionID`. |
1008	| `view` | Always `thread.detail` for Thread Detail snapshots. |
1009	| `threadID` | Thread represented by the snapshot. |
1010	| `epoch` | Relay projection epoch. New epoch replaces local ledger. |
1011	| `seq` | Monotonic update sequence inside `epoch`. |
1012	| `snapshotID` | Unique snapshot payload id for diagnostics. |
1013	| `sourceWatermark` | Upstream Codex history/live point normalized by relay. |
1014	| `scope` | `thread` or `window`. |
1015	| `viewParamsKey` | Canonical key for the relay-filtered view this snapshot proves. |
1016	| `window` | Required when `scope` is `window`; otherwise null. |

1020	
1021	Window snapshots use this `window` shape:
1022	
1023	```json
1024	{
1025	  "order": "displayOrderKeyAscending",
1026	  "offset": 0,
1027	  "limit": 250,
1028	  "firstDisplayOrderKey": "9998239345599999|...",
1029	  "lastDisplayOrderKey": "9998239345601234|...",
1030	  "completeBefore": true,
1031	  "completeAfter": false
1032	}

1034	
1035	Client rules for `scope: "window"`:
1036	
1037	- If any `window` field is missing, the snapshot is invalid and the client must
1038	  request `thread/detail/resync`.
1039	- Replace only rows for the same `threadID` whose `displayOrderKey` is between
1040	  `firstDisplayOrderKey` and `lastDisplayOrderKey`, inclusive.
1041	- Retain rows outside that key range.
1042	- Delete rows inside that key range when they are absent from the snapshot.
1043	- `completeBefore` and `completeAfter` describe whether more rows exist before
1044	  or after the returned key range in display order.
1045	- Do not infer bounds from row count, `offset`, or `nextCursor` alone.

1142	| `kind` | Required fields |
1143	| --- | --- |
1144	| `snapshot` | `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `identityVersion`, `projectionEngineVersion`, `sourceHostID`, `view`, `threadID`, `epoch`, `seq`, `scope`, `viewParamsKey`, `rows`, `complete` |
1145	| `upsert` | `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `identityVersion`, `projectionEngineVersion`, `sourceHostID`, `view`, `threadID`, `epoch`, `seq`, `viewParamsKey`, `rows` |
1146	| `delete` | `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `identityVersion`, `projectionEngineVersion`, `sourceHostID`, `view`, `threadID`, `epoch`, `seq`, `viewParamsKey`, `projectionIDs` |
1147	| `heartbeat` | `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `identityVersion`, `projectionEngineVersion`, `sourceHostID`, `view`, optional `threadID`, `epoch`, `seq`, `viewParamsKey`, `freshness` |
1148	| `resyncRequired` | `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `identityVersion`, `projectionEngineVersion`, `sourceHostID`, `view`, `threadID`, `epoch`, `seq`, `viewParamsKey`, `reason` |

1150	Client update rules:
1151	
1152	- Ignore updates whose `epoch` is not the active epoch.
1153	- Ignore updates whose `seq` is less than or equal to the last applied sequence
1154	  for that epoch.
1155	- Reject updates whose `projectionEngineVersion` differs from the active
1156	  epoch's engine version.
1157	- Reject updates whose `viewParamsKey` differs from the active view.
1158	- A new `epoch` means the client drops the old projection ledger for that
1159	  thread and applies the new snapshot.
1160	- `snapshot` replaces the declared snapshot `scope`.
1161	- `upsert` inserts or replaces rows by exact `projectionID`.
1162	- `delete` removes rows by exact `projectionID`.
1163	- `resyncRequired` marks the view stale and requires `thread/detail/resync`.
1164	
1165	Epoch and watermark rules:
1166	
1167	- `epoch` changes when the relay starts a new detail subscription, changes
1168	  `identityVersion`, detects unrecoverable upstream sequence loss, or
1169	  serves an explicit `thread/detail/resync` after stale state.
1170	- `seq` starts at `1` inside each epoch and increases for every detail
1171	  update.
1172	- `snapshotID` is diagnostic only; it is not row identity.
1173	- `sourceWatermark` is freshness proof and log context; Swift must not use it as
1174	  row identity.

1176	### Identity Rules
1177	
1178	Supported turn-item rows:
1179	
1180	```text
1181	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/row:<rowRole>
1182	```
1183	
1184	Server request rows without item identity:
1185	
1186	```text
1187	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/request:<requestID>/row:request
1188	```
1189	
1190	Request rows with turn/item identity but no known item row role:
1191	
1192	```text
1193	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/request:<requestID>/row:request
1194	```
1195	
1196	Diagnostics:
1197	
1198	```text
1199	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/diagnostic:<stableHash>/row:unknown
1200	```
1201	
1202	Thread-level system rows:
1203	
1204	```text
1205	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/system:<systemEventKind>/<sourceSequenceOrTimestamp>
1206	```
1207	
1208	Initial `systemEventKind` values:
1209	
1210	- `threadStatusChanged`
1211	- `threadClosed`
1212	- `identityGap`
1213	- `identityConflict`
1214	- `resyncRequired`
1215	- `upstreamRecovered`
1216	
1217	`stableHash` is SHA-256 over non-secret structural fields only:
1218	
1219	```text
1220	identityVersion
1221	sourceHostID
1222	threadID
1223	raw method or item type
1224	candidate turnID
1225	candidate itemID
1226	candidate requestID
1227	identity error code
1228	```
1229	
1230	It must not include prompt text, transcript text, delta text, command output,
1231	raw audio, bearer tokens, or full JSON payloads.
1232	
1233	No supported message-like row may use `UUID()` or `crypto.randomUUID()` as
1234	visible identity. Identity gaps and conflicts must become diagnostics or
1235	`resyncRequired`, not normal visible message rows.
1236	
1237	Identity lookup precedence:
1238	
1239	| Source | `turnID` | `itemID` |
1240	| --- | --- | --- |
1241	| `thread/turns/list` item | `turn.id`, `turn.turnId`, `turn.turnID` | `item.id` |
1242	| live delta | `params.turnId`, `params.turnID` | `params.itemId`, `params.itemID` |
1243	| `item/started` or `item/completed` | `params.turnId`, `params.turnID`, `params.turn.id`, `params.item.turnId`, `params.item.turnID` | `params.itemId`, `params.itemID`, `params.item.id` |
1244	
1245	Server request identity:
1246	
1247	| Field | Source |
1248	| --- | --- |
1249	| `threadID` | `params.threadId` |
1250	| `requestID` | JSON-RPC request `id` |
1251	| `turnID` | optional `params.turnId`, then `params.turnID` |
1252	| `itemID` | optional `params.itemId`, then `params.itemID` |
1253	
1254	If two present aliases disagree, the relay must emit `resyncRequired` or a
1255	diagnostic row.

1257	Supported live delta methods:
1258	
1259	| Method | `rowRole` | `renderKind` | `visibility` | Text field |
1260	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
1261	| `item/agentMessage/delta` | `agentMessage` | `agentMessage` | `message` | `params.delta` |
1262	| `item/plan/delta` | `plan` | `agentMessage` | `thinking` | `params.delta` |

1280	### Ordering And Accessibility
1281	
1282	The app sorts Thread Detail rows by `displayOrderKey` ascending and does not
1283	rebuild ordering from raw turn/item fields.
1284	
1285	`displayOrderKey` format:
1286	
1287	```text
1288	<invertedActivityMillis>|<turnOrder>|<invertedItemOrder>|<invertedRowOrder>|<safeProjectionID>
1289	```
1290	
1291	Where:
1292	
1293	- `invertedActivityMillis = 9999999999999999 - UnixEpochMilliseconds(activityTime)`,
1294	  left-padded to 16 digits.
1295	- `turnOrder` is left-padded to 10 digits, with `0` as the newest turn in the
1296	  detail window.
1297	- `invertedItemOrder = 9999999999 - itemOrder`, left-padded to 10 digits.
1298	- `invertedRowOrder = 9999999999 - rowOrder`, left-padded to 10 digits.
1299	- `safeProjectionID` uses `AutomationID.safeSegment` escaping.
1300	
1301	Worked example:
1302	
1303	```text
1304	9998239345599999|0000000042|9999999999|9999999999|host%3Aamir-m5%2Fthread%3A019e...%2Fturn%3At1%2Fitem%3Ai1%2Frow%3AuserMessage
1305	```
1306	
1307	Accessibility IDs use the same safe-segment rule:
1308	
1309	```text
1310	codexdock.session.message.<safe(projectionID)>
1311	codexdock.session.request.<safe(projectionID)>
1312	```
1313	
1314	The safe segment rule keeps ASCII letters, ASCII digits, `-`, `.`, and `_`,
1315	percent-encodes every other UTF-8 byte as uppercase `%XX`, and uses `_` for an
1316	empty segment.
1317	
1318	### Render State
1319	
1320	`renderState` is state on the same `projectionID`, not a second identity axis.
1321	
1322	Allowed values:
1323	
1324	- `streaming`: partial text from a live delta.
1325	- `live`: full live item or request not yet confirmed by canonical history.
1326	- `settled`: canonical history has confirmed the row.
1327	- `stale`: relay knows the row may be outdated while waiting for resync.
1328	- `diagnostic`: non-message diagnostic row.
1329	
1330	Allowed transitions:
1331	
1332	```text
1333	streaming -> live -> settled
1334	streaming -> settled
1335	live -> settled
1336	any non-diagnostic -> stale -> settled
1337	diagnostic -> diagnostic
1338	```
1339	
1340	An invalid transition must not create a new `projectionID`. The relay should upsert
1341	the same `projectionID` with the correct state or request resync.
1342

1344	
1345	Every `ThreadDetailUpdateDTO` carries `projectionEngineVersion`, `epoch`, and
1346	monotonic `seq`.

17	## Historical Bottom Line
18	
19	The original drift was real. Before the single-source implementation, the
20	generated Dock card contract kept the JSON payload shape aligned between relay
21	and Swift, but it did not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time,
22	row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.
23	
24	The exact pre-fix failure mode was: Dock cards were built from thread-level
25	`thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work could
26	live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. The implemented fix folds
27	those inputs through the canonical relay card projection before any Dock or
28	Archive card stream is emitted.
29	
30	Implementation plan: [Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan](CODEX_DOCK_DATA_CONTRACT_SINGLE_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md).

201	### Undocumented Contract Gaps
202	
203	These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:
204	
205	1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
206	2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
207	3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
208	4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
209	5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
210	6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
211	7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
212	8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
213	9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
214	10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
215	11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.
216	12. Contract checks protect only a small fixture set and generated Swift text. They do not run full JSON Schema validation against broad runtime examples.

348	## Drift Inventory
349	
350	| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
351	| --- | --- | --- |
352	| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
353	| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
354	| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
355	| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
356	| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
357	| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
358	| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
359	| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
360	| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
361	| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |
362	
363	## Tests That Encode Current Behavior
364	
365	These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:
366	
367	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
368	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
369	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
370	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
371	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
372	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
373	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
374	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
375	- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
376	- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.
377	
378	## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard
379	
380	This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.
381	
382	The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:
383	
384	1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
385	2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
386	3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
387	4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
388	5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
389	6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.
390	
391	## Verdict
392	
393	The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.
394	
395	The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

1363	
1364	## Bottom Line
1365	
1366	The architecture is simple: Codex Dock must have one production truth path for
1367	live state, and every important claim about freshness must be proven over time.
1368	
1369	The client must not be asked to guess whether a connected socket means current
1370	data. The relay must own app-server decoding, card truth, freshness,
1371	completeness, order, and stream liveness. The client renders that truth and
1372	requests rebuilds when the relay's stream identity changes or falls behind.
1373	
1374	The testing strategy is also simple: static snapshots are useful, but they are
1375	not proof that the app works. The proof of record is live convergence:
1376	
1377	```text
1378	real or controlled app-server state changes
1379	  -> relay projection and subscriptions
1380	  -> Swift stream/session clients
1381	  -> rendered iPhone UI samples over time
1382	  -> retained machine-readable reports with lag budgets
1383	```
1384	
1385	The repo already has much of the live-proof harness. The missing architecture is
1386	that this proof is opt-in, unscheduled, ungated, and partly underspecified. That
1387	is why stale-update bugs can ship while tests pass.
1388	
1389	## Canonical Principles
1390	
1391	### P1. One Owner Per Fact
1392	
1393	Every client-visible fact has exactly one production owner.
1394	
1395	| Fact | Canonical owner | Forbidden second owner |
1396	| --- | --- | --- |
1397	| Dock and Archive card existence | Relay `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams | Swift local metadata, diagnostics, preview fixtures, raw app-server routes |
1398	| Card order and recency | Pre-cutover relay `orderKey` / `activityAtMs`; projection cutover relay `displayOrderKey` | Swift timestamp inference, pins, row text, latest rendered message |
1399	| Card freshness and completeness | Relay freshness/completeness fields | Socket connectivity, HTTP diagnostics, host test success |
1400	| Human-only filtering | Relay view params, with Swift defensive filter only as invalid-data guard | Client-side list reconstruction from broad raw thread routes |
1401	| Thread Detail history | Pre-cutover `thread/read includeTurns:false` plus fully paged `thread/turns/list`; projection cutover `thread/detail/*` rows | Dock cards, raw card summaries, partial resume payloads |
1402	| Thread Detail liveness | Pre-cutover focused `thread/resume`; projection cutover `thread/detail/*` epoch/seq/heartbeat/resync | Socket state alone |
1403	| Local labels, rails, pins | Swift local metadata | Relay/card truth fields |
1404	
1405	Local metadata may decorate visible rows. It must never create a row, change
1406	card order, mark data fresh, change status, change summary, or resurrect a row
1407	that the relay no longer emits.
1408	
1409	### P2. Liveness Must Be Re-Proven
1410	
1411	A connected WebSocket is not proof that the data is current.
1412	
1413	Every stateful relay-owned stream or session must have an identity:
1414	
1415	- Pre-cutover Dock and Archive streams: `epoch`, `seq`, and
1416	  `stateGeneration`. Projection cutover streams: `epoch`, `seq`,
1417	  `identityVersion`, `sourceHostID`, and `viewParamsKey`.
1418	- Pre-cutover Thread Detail live session: relay downstream session generation
1419	  plus the active upstream `thread/resume` binding. Projection cutover Thread
1420	  Detail stream: `thread/detail/*` epoch/seq/heartbeat/resync state.
1421	- Realtime transcription: transcription `sessionId` plus sequence acceptance.
1422	
1423	When that identity changes, the missing state must be rebuilt in an observable
1424	way:
1425	
1426	- Dock and Archive must resubscribe or resync.
1427	- Pre-cutover Thread Detail must rehydrate from history before trusting live
1428	  deltas again. Projection cutover replaces that phone-facing rehydrate with
1429	  `thread/detail/resync` or a replacement projection snapshot.
1430	- The UI must show stale/partial/reconnecting when freshness is not proven.
1431	
1432	No production path may silently recover a relay upstream session while leaving
1433	the phone thinking its old stream is still complete.
1434	
1435	### P3. Proof Is Over-Time Convergence
1436	
1437	Proof means the rendered client stays converged with actual source state over a
1438	duration and within a lag budget.
1439	
1440	The following are not enough:
1441	
1442	- a static fixture that renders once;
1443	- a fake Swift stream that manually yields a good payload;
1444	- a one-shot `dock/subscribe`;
1445	- `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`, or `/syncz`;
1446	- a green `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'` when the displayed sync proof
1447	  skipped because its config file was absent.
1448	
1449	Those checks can be useful, but they are lower-tier evidence. They do not prove
1450	the live system is current.
1451	
1452	## Target Architecture
1453	
1454	### Rule 1. Phone Uses Relay Only
1455	
1456	The phone connects to the Dock relay on `:4510`, not to the raw authenticated
1457	app-server on `:4500`.
1458	
1459	Allowed normal phone paths:
1460	
1461	- relay WebSocket for `initialize`, `dock/*`, `archive/*`, Thread Detail,
1462	  composer commands, server requests, and transcription;
1463	- relay-provided host config such as `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`,
1464	  `home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`, LAN hostname, or LAN IP.
1465	
1466	Forbidden normal phone paths:
1467	
1468	- raw app-server `:4500`;
1469	- raw app-server bearer tokens on device;
1470	- phone-side `thread/list`, `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/search`, or broad
1471	  state routes used to rebuild cards;
1472	- relay SQLite/debug/state routes as card truth.
1473	
1474	### Rule 2. Relay Owns Card Truth
1475	
1476	The relay is the only production card-truth owner for Dock and Archive.
1477	
1478	The relay owns:
1479	
1480	- app-server history reads;
1481	- live loaded-session scans;
1482	- human-started filtering;
1483	- latest-activity proof;
1484	- card normalization;
1485	- SQLite materialization;
1486	- stream sequence and snapshot generation;
1487	- freshness and completeness;
1488	- `dock/update` and `archive/update` deltas.
1489	
1490	Swift owns:
1491	
1492	- rendering;
1493	- pre-cutover grouping/filtering/searching of relay rows; after projection
1494	  cutover, any filter/search that changes the visible row set is a relay
1495	  `viewParams` value with a matching `viewParamsKey`;
1496	- local decorative metadata;
1497	- resync/resubscribe behavior when the relay stream contract says state is
1498	  incomplete, stale, mismatched, or behind.
1499	
1500	Swift must not reconstruct card truth from Thread Detail history or local
1501	metadata.
1502	
1503	### Rule 3. Relay Owns Recency
1504	
1505	Dock and Archive order are relay-owned. The client renders relay order.
1506	
1507	The client must not infer row recency from:
1508	
1509	- latest visible message;
1510	- first message;
1511	- pinned status;
1512	- local label;
1513	- local rail;
1514	- Thread Detail events;
1515	- raw timestamps from a side route.
1516	
1517	This prevents the same user-facing bug from reappearing under a new local
1518	projection.
1519	
1520	### Rule 4. Thread Detail Uses One History Path
1521	
1522	Pre-cutover rule:
1523	
1524	Thread Detail history is:
1525	
1526	```text
1527	thread/read includeTurns:false
1528	  -> thread/turns/list until nextCursor is empty
1529	  -> thread/resume excludeTurns:true
1530	```
1531	
1532	For user-visible detail completeness, `thread/turns/list` must request
1533	`itemsView:"full"` on the detail path.
1534	
1535	Projection cutover supersedes this as phone-facing display truth. The relay may
1536	continue using raw `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, and `thread/resume`
1537	internally, but the app consumes `thread/detail/*` projection rows with
1538	`viewParamsKey`, `epoch`, `seq`, heartbeat, and resync semantics.
1539	
1540	Important scoping rule:
1541	
1542	- Thread Detail history requests should use `itemsView:"full"`.
1543	- Relay card-order activity proof calls should not use `itemsView:"full"`.
1544	
1545	The card-order proof needs turn activity timestamps and ordering proof. It does
1546	not need full item bodies. Forcing full item bodies into relay card proof would
1547	mix two separate concerns and increase payload cost.
1548	
1549	Current gap to close during implementation: `ThreadTurnsListParams` does not
1550	currently carry `itemsView`, and relay `listThreadTurns` forwards params as-is.
1551	The sync audit has a `--turn-items-view` flag, but the production detail path
1552	does not currently send the field.
1553	
1554	### Rule 5. Stateful Recovery Must Be Observable
1555	
1556	Stateful paths cannot silently reconnect and keep old state.
1557	
1558	Dock and Archive:
1559	
1560	- reconnecting the transport is not enough;
1561	- `initialize` replay is not enough;
1562	- the subscription must be restored;
1563	- if subscription continuity is not provable, the stream must resubscribe or
1564	  fail into a visible rebuild path.
1565	
1566	Thread Detail:
1567	
1568	- if the downstream phone socket closes, Swift already rehydrates;
1569	- if the relay loses and recreates the upstream `thread/resume` session, the
1570	  phone must also observe a rebuild trigger.
1571	
1572	Consensus decision: close the downstream Thread Detail socket on relay upstream
1573	recovery unless the app-server provides a proven replay guarantee.
1574	
1575	Why close the downstream socket now:
1576	
1577	- Swift already has a tested reconnect/rehydrate path.
1578	- It avoids adding a new protocol message before the architecture is stable.
1579	- It prevents the exact stale-detail failure shape: relay recovered upstream,
1580	  phone stayed connected, and missed history was never replayed.
1581	
1582	Sanctioned projection-identity alternative:
1583	
1584	- `thread/detail/resync` is the sanctioned resync route for the projection
1585	  identity architecture. It must be `threadId`-stamped, generation/epoch
1586	  stamped, added to the relay allow-list, added to Swift DTO handling, added to
1587	  proof tests, and documented in the canonical protocol reference.
1588	
1589	Until projection resync is fully implemented, invisible upstream recovery is
1590	forbidden.
1591	
1592	### Rule 6. Heartbeat Is Real Contract
1593	
1594	Heartbeat is not decorative. It is the stream liveness signal.
1595	
1596	The repo already claims heartbeat in schema, Swift behavior, tests, and README.
1597	The target architecture makes it real instead of leaving a dead contract.
1598	
1599	Relay must emit periodic `kind:"heartbeat"` `dock/update` messages with:
1600	
1601	- `schemaVersion`;
1602	- `view`;
1603	- `epoch`;
1604	- `seq`;
1605	- `stateGeneration` in the pre-cutover card-v2 contract; projection cutover
1606	  replaces this with shared `epoch` and `seq` only;
1607	- `freshness`;
1608	- `lastSyncAt` or equivalent freshness timestamp;
1609	- no row changes.
1610	
1611	The client uses heartbeat to detect:
1612	
1613	- connected-but-unsubscribed streams;
1614	- streams whose relay state is stale even though the socket is open;
1615	- missing updates beyond a bounded timeout.
1616	
1617	Heartbeat must never mark failed data fresh. It may keep the transport alive,
1618	but freshness remains a relay data claim.
1619	
1620	Bounded implementation parameter:
1621	
1622	- heartbeat cadence should align with relay reconcile timing, roughly the
1623	  reconcile interval or a small multiple;
1624	- client stale timeout should be a small multiple of heartbeat cadence;
1625	- exact values belong in constants, not scattered call sites.
1626	
1627	Heartbeat is the canonical liveness contract. Any future non-heartbeat
1628	replacement requires a newer canonical architecture reference and equivalent
1629	proof gates.
1630	
1631	### Rule 7. Freshness Fails Closed
1632	
1633	If the relay cannot prove a source is current, client-visible freshness must be
1634	stale or partial, not fresh.
1635	
1636	This applies to:
1637	
1638	- raw app-server history failures;
1639	- live endpoint failures;
1640	- live lease scan failures;
1641	- validation failures during human-started filtering;
1642	- repeated turn cursors;
1643	- schema or sequence mismatch;
1644	- incomplete windows;
1645	- failed archive reconciliation.
1646	
1647	Current gap to close during implementation: live endpoint failures can be
1648	counted and then effectively hidden by history completeness. The target rule is
1649	that live-scope probe failure marks the relevant scope stale/incomplete and the
1650	client renders that state.
1651	
1652	### Rule 8. Snapshots Cannot Move State Backward
1653	
1654	Snapshots are full replacements, but they are not allowed to overwrite newer
1655	state with older state.
1656	
1657	The pre-cutover card-v2 relay already has monotonic stream sequence material:
1658	
1659	- `seq`;
1660	- `stateGeneration`;
1661	- `epoch`;
1662	- `schemaVersion`.
1663	
1664	Swift must reject stale compatible snapshots when their generation is older
1665	than the current host/view state. A compatible schema is not enough. Projection
1666	cutover keeps the same fail-closed rule, but the continuity fields become the
1667	shared projection `epoch` and `seq`.
1668	
1669	Current gap to close during implementation: Swift currently applies compatible
1670	snapshots without a stale-generation guard.
1671	
1672	### Rule 9. Archive Is A First-Class View
1673	
1674	Archive and Dock are separate views with related but distinct freshness.
1675	
1676	Archive/unarchive mutations must reconcile and publish both affected views:
1677	
1678	- Dock view;
1679	- Archive view.
1680	
1681	Archive freshness must not be accidentally coupled to Dock freshness such that
1682	one scope can stale or freshen the other without proof.
1683	
1684	Current gap to close during implementation: archive mutation scheduling is
1685	drift-prone because the mutation ingestion path schedules generic reconciliation
1686	but does not make Archive convergence a first-class invariant.
1687

1738	- proof commands that skip and still let the run be interpreted as freshness

1744	## Edge And Exception Matrix
1745	
1746	| Scenario | Required behavior | Proof surface |
1747	| --- | --- | --- |
1748	| Dock WebSocket reconnects | `dock/subscribe` is restored or stream fails into visible rebuild | Swift stream test plus real relay soak |
1749	| `dock/update` params missing | Treat as stream corruption; resync/fail, not silent ignore | Swift unit plus relay malformed update test |
1750	| Sequence gap | Request `dock/resync` and converge | Swift stream test plus relay integration |
1751	| Epoch mismatch | Request resync and do not apply stale delta | Swift stream test |
1752	| Schema mismatch | Request resync/fail loudly | Swift stream test plus contract test |
1753	| Older compatible snapshot | Reject if generation is older than current state | Swift unit plus relay delayed snapshot scenario |
1754	| Heartbeat arrives | Update liveness/freshness without row mutation | Swift unit plus relay integration |
1755	| Heartbeat stops | Mark stream stale/reconnect within timeout | controlled simulator scenario |
1756	| Raw app-server history down | Relay marks scope stale/partial; UI does not claim fresh | relay integration plus UI proof |
1757	| Live endpoint down | Live scope fails closed; UI shows stale/partial | controlled `source-refresh` / live failure scenario |
1758	| Cold relay SQLite | UI can show empty/partial only with explicit freshness state | relay integration |
1759	| Stale SQLite | Reconcile or show stale; do not present old cache as fresh | soak comparing long-lived stream vs fresh snapshot |
1760	| Partial window | UI marks partial and catch-up completes or restarts | Swift unit plus controlled large-list scenario |
1761	| Large delta fallback | Snapshot fallback preserves monotonic generation | relay integration plus Swift table test |
1762	| Duplicate card IDs | Reject safely; do not crash through `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` | Swift unit |
1763	| Non-human upsert for human card | Delete/resync or reject; do not leave stale human card | relay contract plus Swift table test |
1764	| Archive mutation | Dock and Archive both reconcile and publish relevant updates | relay integration plus UI archive scenario |
1765	| Archive failure | UI surfaces action failure and does not fabricate row state | Swift store test plus relay scenario |
1766	| Host alias/identity change | Resolve configured/stream/logical host identity without duplicating rows | Swift host identity tests |
1767	| Relay host ID changes cache scope | Prune or invalidate old host rows explicitly | relay state-store test |
1768	| Pre-cutover Thread Detail initial load | `thread/read`, full paged `thread/turns/list`, then `thread/resume`; projection cutover replaces this phone-facing path with `thread/detail/*` projection rows | ThreadDetailStore tests plus sync audit detail probe before cutover; projection proof after cutover |
1769	| Thread Detail repeated cursor | Fail loudly; do not spin or silently truncate | ThreadDetailStore test |
1770	| Thread Detail upstream recovery | Close downstream or send sanctioned resync; Swift rehydrates | relay integration plus UI detail scenario |
1771	| Missing `threadId` in detail notification | Drop or classify explicitly; request-card resolution must not vanish silently | ThreadDetailStore test |
1772	| Multiple active turns | Preserve all visible activity or define single-active-turn UI explicitly | Thread detail event test |
1773	| Server request stale generation | Reject response from stale generation | relay integration |
1774	| `serverRequest/resolved` | Clear matching request card; define missing-thread behavior | ThreadDetailStore test plus controlled fixture |
1775	| Background/foreground | Rehydrate or resync; do not trust stale in-memory state | Swift lifecycle test plus simulator proof |
1776	| Realtime transcription disconnect | Transcription state closes without mutating Dock/Detail truth | voice tests |
1777	| Config rewrite while app runs | Existing streams close/reload or UI exposes old config explicitly | host registry/store test |
1778	| Docs command drift | Doc command gate fails on unsupported flags/deleted scripts | doc-command gate |

1780	## Testing Methodology
1781	
1782	The proof system has six tiers. Lower tiers are necessary, but they cannot
1783	replace higher tiers.
1784	
1785	### Tier A. Contract And Drift Gates
1786	
1787	Purpose: keep protocol surfaces aligned before runtime.
1788	
1789	Required gates:
1790	
1791	- current card contract checks;
1792	- route registry/dispatch parity;
1793	- Swift `AppServerMethods` parity with allowed relay routes;
1794	- schema version parity across JSON schema, relay emission, and Swift constants;
1795	- generated DTO staleness check;
1796	- proof-result schema validation;
1797	- executable doc-command gate.
1798	
1799	Candidate commands:
1800	
1801	```bash
1802	rtk npm run contract:check
1803	rtk npm run test:relay
1804	```
1805	
1806	New target direction: add one CI-safe aggregate target that runs all fast drift
1807	gates without simulator or physical device dependency.
1808	
1809	### Tier B. Swift State Tests
1810	
1811	Purpose: prove Swift state machines handle known events correctly.
1812	
1813	These tests can use fake streams, but they must be labeled as merge/state proof,
1814	not live proof.
1815	
1816	Coverage required:
1817	
1818	- snapshot, delta, heartbeat;
1819	- schema/epoch/sequence mismatch;
1820	- resync behavior;
1821	- stale snapshot rejection;
1822	- duplicate card IDs;
1823	- partial window catch-up;
1824	- missing update params;
1825	- Thread Detail pagination;
1826	- Thread Detail rehydrate on reconnect and foreground;
1827	- server request and resolution behavior;
1828	- archive action state transitions.
1829	
1830	Representative commands:
1831	
1832	```bash
1833	rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
1834	rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
1835	rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
1836	```
1837	
1838	Interpretation rule: passing Tier B means Swift can handle supplied events. It
1839	does not prove real relay delivery over time.
1840	
1841	### Tier C. Relay Integration Tests
1842	
1843	Purpose: prove real relay behavior with fake or controlled upstreams.
1844	
1845	Coverage required:
1846	
1847	- `dock/subscribe` returns canonical snapshot;
1848	- server state mutation emits `dock/update`;
1849	- multi-subscriber updates;
1850	- delete-only delta;
1851	- `dock/resync`;
1852	- Archive mutation emits Dock and Archive convergence;
1853	- live failure fails closed;
1854	- heartbeat is emitted;
1855	- stale snapshot/generation behavior;
1856	- route allow-list rejects unsupported paths.
1857	
1858	Representative command:
1859	
1860	```bash
1861	rtk npm run test:relay
1862	```
1863	
1864	Interpretation rule: passing Tier C proves relay protocol behavior below the UI.
1865	It does not prove the Swift app rendered the update.
1866	
1867	### Tier D. Real Relay Client-Path Soak
1868	
1869	Purpose: prove long-lived relay streams stay converged with fresh snapshots over
1870	time.
1871	
1872	Required properties:
1873	
1874	- long-lived `dock/subscribe`;
1875	- periodic fresh `dock/subscribe`;
1876	- comparison of long-lived stream state against fresh snapshot;
1877	- forced `dock/resync`;
1878	- detail probe that runs `thread/read`, full paged `thread/turns/list`, and
1879	  `thread/resume`;
1880	- lag budget;
1881	- retained JSON and Markdown reports.
1882	
1883	Representative command family:
1884	
1885	```bash
1886	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs --mode soak --client-path-only --force-dock-resync --max-stream-lag-ms 2000
1887	```
1888	
1889	This is a command family, not the exact exhaustive invocation. The runbook owns
1890	the full duration, sample interval, detail, and host parameters, and the
1891	doc-command gate must keep that runbook executable.
1892	
1893	Current doc drift to fix during implementation: older docs mention unsupported
1894	or deleted command surfaces such as `--exhaustive` and deleted parity scripts.
1895	The doc-command gate must make that impossible to miss.

2002	| --- | --- |

2004	| Relay protocol, card DTO, stream, Thread Detail, or proof harness change | Tier A/B/C plus Tier E controlled matrix |
2005	| Daily/nightly on a capable Mac | Tier D soak plus Tier E controlled matrix |
2006	| Before claiming simulator behavior fixed | Tier E on `iPhone 17` |
2007	| Before claiming phone behavior fixed | Tier F |
2008	| Before changing docs/runbooks | Doc-command gate plus affected referenced commands in dry-run or real mode |

2011	
2012	- `scripts/dock-relay*.mjs`;
